title: Packers list DL Javon Hargrave as doubtful, add CB Benjamin St-Juste to injury report
description: The Packers likely won't have DL Javon Hargrave against the Jets, while CB Benjamin St-Juste was added to the injury report on Friday and is questionable.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers listed veteran defensive tackle Javon Hargrave as doubtful to play against the New York Jets in Week 2 as he works through the league's concussion protocol. Hargrave suffered symptoms to start the week, was placed in the concussion protocol and did not practice on Thursday or Friday.

The Packers also ruled out defensive tackle Warren Brinson, who will miss his second straight game due to a calf injury.

The defensive line is dealing with two injuries, but Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan, Jonathan Ford and Anthony Campbell are all healthy and available to play.

The Packers listed four players as questionable to play: edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (concussion), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) and left guard Aaron Banks (knee). St-Juste, a backup at corner, was added to the injury report on Friday with a new injury. He was limited in the final practice of the week. As was the case last week, Banks practiced during all three practices this week, but he is questionable to play and is likely a game-time decision.

Van Ness is still going through the concussion protocol but was able to practice each day this week. He will need to pass the protocol to play Sunday.

QUESTIONABLE: EDGE Lukas Van Ness, CB Benjamin St-Juste, RT Zach Bako-Bewele, LG Aaron Banks

Linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper does not have a status designation and will return after missing Week 1 with an Achilles injury.

The Jets ruled out four players: safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, receiver Omar Cooper Jr., running back/returner Kene Nwangwu and edge rusher Joseph Ossai. Edge rusher Will McDonald IV is questionable to play but should be good to go Sunday, per Aaron Glenn.

title: Camilla Orlando previews Spain clash in Under-20 World Cup quarters
description: The Women’s U-20 National Team is ready for another challenge at the World Cup. This Friday (18), the team wrapped up its preparations for the clash against Spain in the quarterfinals of the tournam...
fullText:
The Women's U-20 National Team is ready for another challenge at the World Cup. This Friday (18), the team wrapped up its preparations for the clash against Spain in the quarterfinals of the tournament. On the eve of the match, head coach Camilla Orlando analyzed the opponents' characteristics and shared her expectations for the game.

"It will be a very challenging match. I would describe it as a chess game. Spain really likes to keep possession and control space, just like we do. It will be a very difficult match, like all the others, but it certainly has a different flavor because it's the quarterfinals," said the coach.

For Camilla, preparation for the clash involves maintaining the principles that have guided the team throughout the competition. The coach highlighted concentration and discipline as key factors in facing the Spanish side, without giving up Brazil's attacking style.

"We have to keep doing our work, with a lot of focus, discipline, and joy. Our players have been able to bring all of Brazil's joy, our way of playing with a lot of grit, so I don't think we need to do anything differently. We'll maintain consistency and attention to detail, but we want to keep showing our attacking game with the desire to score at every moment," Camilla added.

The match between Brazil and Spain will take place this Saturday (19) at 1:30 p.m. Brasília time, at Arena Sosnowiec in Poland. The winner of the match will advance to the semifinals of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup.

title: Rays' 'fatal flaw' for MLB postseason involves one-third of their lineup
description: These three lineup spots could prove to be a season-ender for the Rays.
fullText:
Rays' 'fatal flaw' for MLB postseason involves one-third of their lineup originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Tampa Bay Rays have clinched a spot in the MLB postseason and, now in the final week and a half of the season, are seeking the AL East title.

But once the postseason starts, regardless of their final seeding, it's going to be a tricky field, with the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox being their top competition.

In the postseason, there is one major flaw the Rays cannot afford to succumb to. As ESPN's David Schoenfield noted, the Rays have a flaw with one-third of their lineup that could make a deep postseason run a bit challenging to accomplish.

"Tampa Bay Rays. Fatal flaw: Lineup depth (24th in OPS from 7-8-9 slots in lineup)," Schoenfield writes. "... But the bottom third of the lineup has been an issue for most of the season."

While the Rays will need Junior Caminero to lead this offense alongside Yandy Diaz, Jonathan Aranda, and Liam Hicks, the bottom third of the lineup is important as well.

While Hicks, Caminero, Aranda, and Diaz are good starters, there are plenty of question marks elsewhere in the lineup. Chandler Simpson is an X-factor, so while his overall offense might not be as elite as some others, his speed makes a big difference.

Richard Palacios, Ryan Vilade, Jorge Mateo, Taylor Walls, Cedric Mullins, Jake Fraley, Jonny DeLuca, and Victor Mesa Jr. are the other options currently on the roster for the final four slots in the lineup.

MORE: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski makes all kinds of MLB history with 1,000 pitches of 100 mph

While many of these hitters have had their moments, the fact that their 7-8-9 hitters have put up the 24th-best OPS in the big leagues this season is something to worry about.

There's a chance that the hitters in those spots of the order figure things out in the postseason, but if the bottom third of the lineup struggles, it's going to be hard to score runs in October.

This issue is a "fatal flaw" according to Schoenfield, and while that might be a bit of a stretch, the struggles from one-third of the lineup are something that could end up sinking the Rays' chances this season.

title: Top Canadiens Players To Watch In Preseason Action
description: The Montreal Canadiens are set to face the Toronto Maple Leafs in simultaneous games this weekend, with the split teams […]
fullText:
The Montreal Canadiens are set to face the Toronto Maple Leafs in simultaneous games this weekend, with the split teams playing at the Bell Centre in Montreal, as well as the Scotiabank Arena in Toronto.

Despite the logistical challenges of running concurrent games, the arrangement will give Habs fans a chance to see every NHL hopeful in action, including several players aiming to either make the team or improve their standing within the organization.

The Canadiens have already divided their 57 training-camp players into three groups, with Group A set to face the Maple Leafs in Quebec and Group B playing the away game in Ontario.

Forwards: Owen Beck, Alex Belzile, Cole Caufield, Lucas Condotta, Jared Davidson, Ivan Demidov, Oliver Kapanen, Chris Kreider, Sasha Pastujov, Juraj Slafkovsky, Nick Suzuki, Tyler Thorpe.

Defencemen: Alexandre Carrier, Aiden Dubinsky, Lane Hutson, Luke Mittelstadt, Owen Protz, Ethan Samson, Jayden Struble, Arber Xhekaj.

Goalies: Jakub Dobes, Jacob Fowler.

Given that this marks the first time the freshly formed first line will face NHL-level competition, all eyes will be on newcomer Chris Kreider, who is set to play alongside captain Nick Suzuki and sniper Cole Caufield.

While breaking up the former first line, which featured Juraj Slafkovsky on the left wing, carries some risk, there is little doubt that Kreider brings a similar style of play to the mix. He excels at tipping pucks; in fact, no other NHLer has come close to matching his production in that category. Kreider has scored 100 tip-in goals since 2012-13, including 25 over the past three seasons.

Like Slafkovsky, he is a big-bodied forward, but he brings far more experience to the constant battle for prime ice in high-danger scoring areas.

The second line will enjoy a measure of familiarity, with Slafkovsky returning to the wing, Oliver Kapanen centring him, and Demidov serving as the playmaker. Last season the trio controlled over 58 percent of the goals at 5-on-5 (25-18), highly encouraging results given their limited experience. Slafkovsky, then just 21 years old, was the elder statesman of the group. Now a year older and wiser, the Canadiens will look to them to manage games more consistently by tightening their control of shots, expected goals, and high-danger chances.

On the blue line, former University of Minnesota captain Luke Mittelstadt enters the main Canadiens camp with strong momentum after standing out as the top defenceman at the team's rookie camp earlier this month. He was the busiest player in a Montreal uniform and performed well at both ends of the ice under new Laval Rocket head coach Daniel Jacob, who ran the rookie camp.

Josh Nadeau scores his hat trick goal to give the #GoHabsGo a 4-3 lead.

A fantastic play by Luke Mittelstadt to set up the goal. pic.twitter.com/WDwypWkmsA

— Montreal Hockey Now (@MTLhockeynow) September 14, 2026

Forward: Josh Anderson, Brett Berard, Zachary Bolduc, Kirby Dach, Phillip Danault, Jake Evans, Alex Newhook, Alexandre Texier, Hunter McKeown, Filip Mesar, Samuel Poulin, Florian Xhekaj.

Defencemen: Noah Dobson, Adam Engstrom, Braden Hache, Mike Matheson, Kale McCallum, David Reinbacher, Maksymillian Szuber, Reilly Walsh.

Goalies: Kaapo Kahkonen, Samuel Montembeault.

While most of the attention in Group A will focus on the forwards, Group B will feature a battle among defencemen eager to begin their NHL careers in earnest.

David Reinbacher has already put the media on notice, aiming to capitalize on the available minutes while Kaiden Guhle recovers from his latest surgery. The 21-year-old Austrian is typically reserved, but he displayed an elevated level of bravado on Friday afternoon, a promising sign for a player who could use a lasting confidence boost.

Adam Engstrom, by contrast, receives less media attention than other prospects. Yet if judged purely by the numbers, he may edge Reinbacher in NHL readiness. That's hardly surprising, given that Engstrom has already amassed over 200 games of professional experience early in his career. He also outscored every other Laval Rocket defenceman by a rather wide margin last season.

Up front, the forward lines will be packed with players looking to boost their long-term value to the organization, including newly signed winger Zachary Bolduc, centre Kirby Dach, and Frenchman Alexandre Texier. All three enjoyed varying degrees of success in 2025-26, with Texier, in particular, providing excellent secondary scoring in limited minutes.

The Montreal Canadiens versus Toronto Maple Leafs split preseason games are both scheduled for 7 pm ET, on Saturday, September 19.

title: Carson Wentz starting vs. Bears: His career stats and record
description: Carson Wentz will make his first start of the season against Chicago.
fullText:
The Vikings have officially ruled out Kyler Murray for Week 2 against the Bears, which means Carson Wentz will make his first start of the season, and fifth all-time against Chicago.

Fun fact: Wentz has never lost to the Bears.

Sunday will be Wentz's 100th career start in his NFL career, and fourth against the Bears. He faced Chicago once with Washington and three times with Philadelphia. In those four starts, Wentz has a 62.5 completion rate, while averaging 188.8 passing yards with five touchdowns and zero interceptions. His team has won by an average score of 23.5 to 9.5.

2022 @ Chicago (WAS/12-7 W): 12/22, 99 yards, 0 TDs, 2 carries, 2 yards, 3 sacks

2019 vs. Chicago (PHI/22-14 W): 26/39, 239 yards, 1 TD, 4 carries, 15 yards, 4 sacks

2017 vs. Chicago (PHI/31-3 W): 23/36, 227 yards, 3 TD, 5 carries, 29 yards, 1 sack

2016 @ Chicago (PHI/29-14 W): 21/34, 190 yards, 1 TD, 6 carries, 10 yards, 2 sacks

Ben Johnson showed last season that Chicago is no longer the defense-first franchise that it has been known as for decades. That was even more true in Week 1 with a 59-point explosion. It's fair to assume that Wentz will not receive the same defensive help he has in his four previous matchups with the Bears, so the pressure is on to score points.

Playing at Soldier Field in late September is a lot different than in late fall or early winter. Wentz and the Vikings still have to face the elements with potential for rain and gusty wind, although it's still too hard to predict exactly what the weather will be on Sunday afternoon.

Wentz looked solid when he came in for Murray in Week 1, finishing 12-of-19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns. Depending on the weather, Minnesota might need more from its QB against Johnson's high-powered offense.

Sunday projects as a high-level chess match between Johnson and Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, who are widely considered two of the best play callers in the sport. Wentz will look to win his 50th career start and break his .500 career record as a starter.

title: Saints' plan to keep Lamar Jackson in the pocket presents a major gamble
description: Saints' Carl Granderson wants Lamar Jackson kept in the pocket, but the Ravens quarterback remains among the NFL's most dangerous passers
fullText:
The New Orleans Saints know that letting Lamar Jackson escape the pocket can turn a productive defensive snap into an explosive play. Saints defensive end Carl Granderson believes discipline will be central to New Orleans' plan for containing the Baltimore Ravens quarterback Sunday at M&T Bank Stadium.

"We can't overthink it," Granderson said, via the NOF Network. "We just gotta go into the game, keep him in the pocket and play our game."

The approach is understandable, but keeping Jackson between the tackles does not eliminate the most dangerous parts of Baltimore's offense. The two-time NFL MVP has become one of the league's most efficient pocket passers and can punish defenses that get too focused on his running ability. Jackson completed 17 of 25 passes for 324 yards and one touchdown in Baltimore's 41-23 victory over Indianapolis. He averaged 13 yards per attempt, avoided an interception, and threw for more yards than in any game during the 2025 season.

#Saints DE Carl Granderson on containing #Ravens QB Lamar Jackson:

"We can't overthink it. We just gotta go into the game, keep him in the pocket and play our game." pic.twitter.com/0uLtFVBrdO

Jackson was also effective when offensive coordinator Declan Doyle placed him under center. He completed six of eight attempts for 114 yards from that alignment, including a 49-yard connection with Zay Flowers off a bootleg concept. His development as a passer predates Doyle's arrival. Jackson threw for 4,172 yards, 41 touchdowns and only four interceptions during his 2024 All-Pro season. He finished with a 119.6 passer rating, showing defenses cannot simply concede the pocket and expect Baltimore's passing game to become less efficient.

New Orleans must maintain rush-lane integrity because Jackson can still change the game as a runner. He converted a third-and-16 against Indianapolis by avoiding two defenders and scrambling for 16 yards. However, Granderson and the Saints cannot become passive while attempting to contain him. Jackson's patience, accuracy, and improved command from the pocket make him just as capable of dissecting a defense without crossing the line of scrimmage.

fullText:

The New Orleans Saints will be facing the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2, and there's a chance two of their key players will be ready to suit up. Chris Olave and Chase Young dealt with some injuries during practice this week that many wanted to keep an eye on. Olave left practice as a precautionary measure due to a hamstring injury, but it's reported that it was nothing serious.

As for Young, he'd been dealing with calf soreness, but everything seems to be fine with him. Both players were able to participate in the final practice before the game and are both listed as questionable, according to Nick Underhill.

It feels like they'll both be on the field for the Ravens game, but anything can change between now and game time.

Olave had a good game against the Detroit Lions in Week, and he led the team in receiving yards. The offense was humming throughout the entire game and put itself in a good position to possibly win the game in the end. The Saints have another tough task this week with the Ravens, as they put up 40 points on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1. They were led by Derrick Henry, who finished the game with three touchdowns.

It's still early in the season, so it's hard to see how the Saints will look, but if their offense can put up points, they should be in good shape.

fullText:
Pirates news: Paul Skenes' inconsistent season draws truth bomb from manager appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

It's no secret that the 2026 campaign has been a roller coaster for Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes. His play has been rather inconsistent, as he's been nowhere near his Cy Young-caliber self all year. While his play has been alarming, manager Don Kelly is not yet ready to hit the panic button.

During a guest appearance on MLB Radio, Kelly praised the 24-year-old right-hander for at least maintaining his work ethic throughout the season. After two incredible years to begin his career, Kelly is impressed with Skenes' approach during what's been considered a down year for the superstar pitcher.

"Paul set the bar so high in his first two years, having a sub-2.00 ERA, winning the Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year," Kelly said. "I think the thing with Paul is the work ethic, the commitment to excellence, how he's continued to push himself, even through the first two years, and certainly this year, in trying to continue to grind to get better. He's been the same guy through all of it.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Continues to work hard, continues to try to make adjustments, and did so as the season went on last year. And then this year, doing the same thing," Kelly continued. "I think that there's been no excuses from him. He's such a pro in how he goes about it, and how he continues to work every single day to maximize his talents, and also go out there and do everything that he can to try to help us win every time he's on the mound."

Although Paul Skenes hasn't been dominant this year, it's not like he's been absolutely dreadful either. His play would still be considered good for most in the league. Through 162.0 innings pitched this season, the three-time All-Star owns a 3.78 ERA and 1.130 WHIP while totaling 185 strikeouts.

He'll have a chance to end the campaign on a high note in one of his final appearances on Friday against the Kansas City Royals. That contest is scheduled to begin at 6:40 p.m. EST and will be the first of a three-game series in Pittsburgh.

title: Patriots vs. Steelers Friday injury report: Carlton Davis III among three questionable
description: Game designations for Week 2 at Gillette Stadium.
fullText:
The New England Patriots will host the Pittsburgh Steelers with uncertainty on the outside.

Cornerback Carlton Davis III has been listed as questionable for the 2026 home opener due to a neck injury, as Mike Vrabel previously told reporters during his Friday press conference.

"I don't want to assume, but he'll be questionable," New England's head coach said of the veteran starter, who has remained a non-participant for three consecutive practices. "We'll have to see how he comes in here tomorrow. We'll continue to evaluate and if the designation changes, we'll update everybody."

Interior offensive lineman Ben Brown and outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones also carry questionable statuses into the weekend, while rookie tackle Dametrious Crownover has been officially ruled out.

Here's the final injury report leading up to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium.

CB Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning, back)

Crownover, the No. 196 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, stayed sidelined throughout preparations because of a knee injury. The reserve tackle out of Texas A&M saw two snaps on special teams during his Patriots debut last week. And for the Steelers, there will be no Porter in the secondary. The fourth-year cornerback missed the first matchup of September and has since been listed for non-injury reasons, conditioning as well as a back ailment.

Brown and Jones logged back-to-back-to-back limited practices in Foxborough before being called questionable. The picture is less clear for Davis as well as a big-bodied wide receiver across the aisle. In the season opener versus the Seattle Seahawks, the veteran cornerback played 49 out of 50 defensive snaps despite briefly departing after making a tackle for no gain in the first quarter at Lumen Field. He was in attendance for Monday's bonus practice before missing Wednesday, Thursday and Friday's sessions.

In the event Davis' questionable status ends up in the inactives, the list of options to join All-Pro Christian Gonzalez on the boundary begin with 2025 waiver claim Charles Woods and team captain Marcus Jones. The depth chart also includes fifth-rounder Karon Prunty and undrafted rookie Channing Canada on the 53-man roster. And Kindle Vildor, now 80 games and 27 starts into his NFL career, resides on the practice squad.

Elsewhere, running back TreVeyon Henderson and linebacker Robert Spillane will go without game statuses after finishing the work week as full participants.

title: Who is new caddie for Alejandrio Tosti at PGA Tour Biltmore Championship second round?
description: PGA Tour golfer Alejandro Tosti got a new caddie, Patrick Talledo, for round two at the Biltmore Championship. Tosti's first caddie quit in round one.
fullText:
Alejandro Tosti returned with a new caddie for the second round of the Biltmore Championship on Sept. 18.

Patrick Talledo is Tosti's new caddie, according to an updated list released by the PGA during the second round.

Tosti needed a new caddie after Cliff Ellis, who he started the tournament, abruptly walked off the 18th green during the first round on Sept. 17. Tosti shot 1-over par 71 in the first round at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove.

Tosti, a 30-year old golfer from Argentina, played in a group with Luke Clanton and Spencer Oxendine and started at 8:59 a.m. from the 10th tee. He was closing out the front nine at the 18th hole when caddie Cliff Ellis dropped the bag, took off his caddie bib and walked off the course.

"He couldn't keep up with eight pars in a row," Totsi joked when reached for comment by Golfweek, referencing his start to the round.

Tosti and Ellis had butted heads during the practice round on Sept. 15, Golfweek said. But Tosti was surprised by Ellis' departure. He thought Ellis was simply using the bathroom when he left the 18th green.

Known to be a fiery competitor, Tosti has admitted publicly in the past that he can sometimes let his emotions get the best of him. He entered this weekend ranked 186th in the FedEx Cup fall standings.

Tosti will teed off his second round from the first hole at 1:49 p.m., looking to avoid the cut line.

fullText:
Chelsea are taking on Brentford at the G Tech, and Jordan Henderson has been a big part of our good performance in the game.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

It's half time in Chelsea's game against Brentford, and while it's not a classic for the neutral, it's a fascinating game.

Chelsea fans were very worried about their team in this match. Brentford are a hard team to break down, and they've done really well against us in the last few years. Given we are without a few key players in midfield and our defence has looked shaky, this was a worrying game.

LONDON, ENGLAND – AUGUST 27: Jordan Henderson of Chelsea arrives at the stadium before the Carabao Cup Second Round match between Chelsea and Luton Town at Stamford Bridge on August 27, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Instead the Blues have been really solid. They haven't created much, but they've got a foothold in the game and stopped it getting away from them. A big part of that has been Jordan Henderson, who is making his debut and has made a great impression.

Henderson is making his debut tonight, a big moment for him and for Chelsea as they try to figure out their midfield depth chart.

title: Rutgers Basketball Lands Four-Star Guard Korey Francis
description: Rutgers adds second four star to 2027 class.
fullText:
Rutgers basketball has landed its second four-star commit and second overall commit of the 2027 recruiting class, as guard Korey Francis has committed to play for the Scarlet Knights, according to Joe Tipton of On3 and his social media pages. His commitment comes after he took an official visit to Piscataway last weekend.

The 6-foot-3, 185-pound guard out of Monsignor Bonner High School in Pennsylvania is ranked No. 129 nationally in the 2027 class by 247 Sports and is the No.108 player in the class according to On3. 247 Sports has him listed as a combo guard while On3 lists him as a point guard. He chose Rutgers over offers from schools like Mississippi State, Seton Hall, Virginia Tech, Xavier, and others.

During the 2025-2026 season, Francis was named the 2025-2026 MaxPreps Pennsylvania High School Basketball Player of the Year. During that season, Francis averaged 21.6 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game for the Friars while shooting 52.3 percent from the field, 36.7 percent from three, and 75.0 percent from the free-throw line, all while helping his team go 24-6 and win the Class 5A State Championship for Pennsylvania.

He joins four-star shooting guard RJ Moore as the only two 2027 commits in the class for Rutgers.

title: Ryan Gerard takes 2-shot lead into weekend at star-studded BMW PGA Championship
description: Ryan Gerard sits atop a star-laden leaderboard after two rounds at the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship.
fullText:
When Brandt Snedeker announced his captain's picks for the U.S. Presidents Cup team, a loud portion of American fans on social media expressed frustration seeing Ryan Gerard's name omitted. There seemed to be a consensus among commenters that Gerard was the victim of a good ol' fashioned snubbing.

But while he had plenty of outraged mouthpieces on the internet, Gerard did not throw himself a pity party. Quite the opposite. He wasn't going to let Snedeker's decision derail his plans for a swing across the pond.

After finishing solo third at the Tour Championship, Gerard took a red-eye to Switzerland for the Omega European Masters, where he finished T-30, and this week, he's in England for the BMW PGA Championship, the DP World Tour's marquee event.

"The DP World Tour is a great tour and we're lucky to have fantastic events like this one that I can come play in what would technically be the offseason on the PGA Tour," Gerard said. "There's a lot of really awesome places outside of the United States that we don't get to go to very often ... It's really, really cool that I have that opportunity, and we're going to take advantage of it."

He's certainly taking advantage of it. Gerard finished birdie-eagle to cap off a bogey-free, 7-under 65 in Friday's second round at Wentworth Club, moving to 12 under for the tournament and taking a two-shot lead into the weekend.

"A really, really solid day of golf," Gerard said. "Conditions at times were pretty difficult with the wind picking up. Wentworth is not easy, with some of these pin locations they like to stick us with during the tournament. You've just got to be really patient, pick your spots ... We did a really good job all day of hitting to the right spots."

American leading the @BMWPGA by two at Wentworth 🇺🇸👀

Ryan Gerard closes with birdie for an exceptional second-round 65 👏 pic.twitter.com/wq9mSrERQW

Speaking of American players who could argue they were snubbed out of a spot on the Presidents Cup team, 2025 U.S. Open champion and three-time PGA Tour winner J.J. Spaun also finds himself in the mix at Wentworth, sitting at 8 under and in a tie for sixth after 36 holes.

"It was disappointing to be left off [the Presidents Cup team]," Spaun said Friday. "I mean, I wasn't really expecting it, to be honest ... I kind of hung my hat on my experience with the Ryder Cup last year. Made it to the Tour Championship this year. I won in San Antonio. I kind of did everything I could. I was the odd man out."

But just like Gerard, Spaun didn't sulk. He got right back in the saddle.

"I wanted to continue to play golf, whether it was going to be here or at the Presidents Cup in Medinah," Spaun said. "I always had this circled, if I didn't get in Medinah. I'm here and I'm just doing what I do, play golf, and do the best that I can."

Gerard and Spaun have the chance to join Billy Horschel and Arnold Palmer as the only Americans to ever win the BMW PGA, but to do so, they'll have to hold off a slew of talented players and season veterans.

Australia's Adam Scott, who will represent the International side next week at the Presidents Cup, is tied for second and will play alongside Gerard in the final pairing Saturday. Plus, three of the four major winners in 2026 are firmly in contention. PGA Champion Aaron Rai is T-4 at 9-under, while Open Champion Ryan Fox is part of a five-way tie for sixth that also includes back-to-back Masters winner Rory McIlroy.

Like Gerard, McIlroy was part of the afternoon wave Friday that had to fight blustery conditions, but he still managed to post a 5-under 67 to follow up his 69 in the opening round. He's looking to win the BMW PGA for the second time in his career.

"[Gerard] has played great, obviously," McIlroy said. "I feel like our side of the draw I think got some of the worst of the conditions ... But four behind isn't too much going into the weekend and I'm excited for the opportunity."

On the other end of the leaderboard, there was some drama involving some fan-favorite Englishmen playing in front of a home crowd. Alex Fitzpatrick stepped up to the 16th tee at 1 over for the tournament, well outside the 2-under cutline. He birdied Nos. 16 and 17, but found himself needing to hole a pitch shot for birdie at the par-5 18th to earn a spot on Saturday's tee sheet. He did exactly that, much to the delight of the gallery.

HOLEOUT TO MAKE THE CUT ON 18 🤯🔥

Incredible pitch-in by Alex Fitzpatrick over the water, and the English fans are amped for their countryman 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚡️ pic.twitter.com/GXlEvaA8gd

Justin Rose, meanwhile, bounced back from a disappointing 73 on Thursday with a 67 on Friday, finishing the second round 3 under and advancing to the weekend. His countryman Tommy Fleetwood (3 over) didn't meet such a fate, nor did American Brooks Koepka (1 over).

And then there was Spanish superstar Jon Rahm, who turned in one of the worst performances of his entire pro career, making 10 bogeys and a pair of double bogeys over 36 holes. He finished 11 over, dead last on the leaderboard among those who actually finished the second round.

There have been six withdrawals at Wentworth this week, including Patrick Reed, who leads the DP World Tour's season-long standings but pulled out of the BMW PGA on Friday, citing an injury.

Nick Stavas is a digital producer and commerce writer for Golfweek. Follow him on X/Twitter (@nickstavas).

title: Cal won't judge its next opponent by its 87-3 loss. Its own offense has work to do
description: Tosh Lupoi's Bears hope to build a winning streak and overwhelm visiting Wagner this weekend, while Stanford heads to Duke and San Jose State has its home opener.
fullText:
While Cal football is heavily favored against a Wagner team that lost 87-3 the previous week, the Bears are not taking their FCS opponents lightly.

"I've learned in 20 years of coaching, the last thing you're doing is allowing the last performance to be the judgment of a team," head coach Tosh Lupoi said Tuesday. Wagner is "top 20 in the FCS in bringing pressure and top 20 in creating TFLs; that's problematic. That's what I'm looking at, and just like us, it's a clean slate moving forward."

And it's not like Cal can afford to take the outcome for granted, given their offensive inconsistencies. Through two games, the Bears offense ranks 86th in the country in points per game (25.3) and 89th in yards per game (357.6). In their 17 possessions since the 8:28 mark in the third quarter of Cal's 45-24 season opener loss to UCLA, the Bears have found the end zone just twice. If not for defensive back Kingston Lopa's fourth-quarter pick-six to take the decisive 21-18 lead, the Bears might have come up short against Syracuse.

It's a problem that falls on offensive coordinator Jordan Somerville, who expressed belief that the offense is capable of much more than what they have shown thus far.

"We still believe that there's no doubt about it; we got an explosive unit," the first-year offensive coordinator said Tuesday. "Fundamentals go back to the basics. Trust our training."

It's not a question of talent. With a quarterback as gifted as Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, surrounded by touted skill position players from the transfer portal, the Bears have the pieces of a potent offense. But it's on Somerville to put it together. And while it's early and there are sure to be some growing pains with a first-time play caller and a sophomore quarterback, Cal invested a lot of money in its offense. At some point this season, the bill has to come due.

But for Lupoi, it's less about the play-calling and more about the execution.

"Jordan Somerville is doing an awesome job. He's open-minded to seeing who we are, how we can utilize our personnel best," Lupoi said. "And when you dive into that film, within the last two weeks, we've had seven balls that … it hits the hands, and it's dropped. We've got to do that at a better level. We can't just be saying, 'Catch the ball,' is a poor coaching point."

Luckily for Cal, Wagner is the perfect kind of opponent to iron out the kinks in the offense. At least, in theory. The Bears will kick off against the Seahawks in Memorial Stadium at 12:30pm PST.

After a thorough 45-6 thrashing by the powerhouse Miami Hurricanes two weeks ago, Stanford heads across the country to Duke with a focus on tightening up their schemes.

"When you look at our first two games, there were times when we lost focus. We lost focus on what our job was. And that starts with me," coach Tavita Pritchard told reporters Wednesday, explaining that the team spent the past two weeks drilling the little things like technique and foot placement.

"I resist the phrase 'get back to the basics,' because I think you should never leave the basics. It's about really making sure the fundamentals of what we do within our systems - offense, defense, and special teams - that we are very detailed in our approach to those things."

The details will have to be up to par as the Cardinal face an electric Blue Devils offense. Sophomore running back Nate Sheppard is second in the country with 374 rushing yards through two games this season. Paired with quarterback Walker Eget, who last season with San Jose State burned the Cardinal defense for 473 yards and three touchdowns, Duke's offense will look to generate big plays against a Stanford defense prone to giving up large gains.

For their own offense, Stanford will turn to quarterback Davis Warren to keep pace with the Blue Devils, which starts by limiting turnovers.

"He's going to have to be really on it this week," Pritchard said. "This defense has created a lot of turnovers, and they won our conference championship game because they had a defense that is opportunistic."

It's a tricky tightrope act - limiting turnovers while staying aggressive against Duke's ball-hawking defense, Pritchard explained, but he trusts Warren to deliver.

"When the opportunities present themselves, he's done a good job of taking those plays where they exist," Pritchard said. "He has to keep living in that space in that balance of protecting the ball but playing with an attacking mindset."

Stanford kicks off against Duke at the Wallace Wade Stadium at 1 p.m. PST, the teams' first meeting since 2012. The Cardinal are 3-1 all-time versus the Blue Devils.

While conference realignment has torn apart some historic rivalries, San Jose State vs. Fresno State remains testy as the two programs meet for the first time since the Bulldogs left the Mountain West for the Pac-12 this past year.

Which is why Spartans head coach Ken Niumatalolo is taking a measured approach.

"We recognize this is our big rivalry game, and we got to do the best we can to get ready. But all you can worry about is between the white lines," Niumatalolo told reporters Thursday, more focused on San Jose State's habit of slow starts the past couple of games. "Obviously it's big for our school and our fans, but if we don't play well, it doesn't matter."

The Spartans will lean on running back Jabari Bates, who's third in the country with 319 rushing yards, as well as quarterback Luke Weaver, who has thrown for 788 yards and three TDs through three games this season.

Despite Niumatalolo downplaying the emotion around this game, he still believes it is important for San Jose State as they try to build a winning streak.

"Going into conference play, we want to continue that positive trend that we're going in," Niumatalolo said. "I know it's going to be hard, but I think this will be monumental for us for the rest of the season. This is a huge game."

San Jose State faces Fresno State in their home opener at 8 p.m. PST.

Kenzo Fukuda is a freelance journalist born and raised in San Francisco. He has covered the Giants, Warriors and Valkyries since 2025, and he previously covered Cal football and women's basketball from 2022-24. You can follow him on X at @kenzofuku

There's more to San Francisco with the Chronicle.

title: Adzic insists he should have been given more game time at Juventus
description: Vasilije Adzic came back to haunt Juventus after facing the Bianconeri with Sassuolo at the weekend, with the midfielder suggesting he deserved more opportunities during his time in Turin.Adzic scored...
fullText:
Vasilije Adzic came back to haunt Juventus after facing the Bianconeri with Sassuolo at the weekend, with the midfielder suggesting he deserved more opportunities during his time in Turin.

Adzic scored a fantastic and important goal against Inter Milan last season, but that effort did not result in many more chances at Juventus. Despite making an impact when called upon, he remained without a regular role in the squad.

When Luciano Spalletti arrived as manager, the gaffer did not fancy Adzic, allowing him to leave on loan this term. Sassuolo also have an option to buy him permanently in the summer, giving the player an opportunity to establish himself away from Turin.

Judging by the way he has performed so far, it would be a surprise if the black and greens did not make the move permanent. His performances have provided him with the platform to show what he can offer when given regular opportunities.

At Juventus, Adzic competed for a place against much better players, but he believes he should have been used more often. The Bianconeri had plenty of options available, making regular appearances difficult to secure.

Juve also did not believe Adzic was mature enough for a bigger role, although his loan spell is revealing the opposite. Regular football has allowed him to demonstrate his ability and continue his development.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

The midfielder could end the season with double figures if he maintains his current form. He also accepts that selection decisions were not within his control, while believing he could have contributed more had he been given additional opportunities.

Speaking via Tuttojuve, Adzic explained why moving to Sassuolo was the sensible decision for his development.

"Maybe at Juve I could have played a little more, or at least I hoped so. Maybe I even deserved it, but these are not decisions that are up to me, so that's fine. At Juventus, I had several good games, and the path I'm on, the decision to come to Sassuolo to get more playing time and prove my worth, was the most sensible choice. Now I intend to give everything for this club."

His performances could now convince Sassuolo to make his move permanent in the summer.

title: Zinedine Zidane confirms Real Madrid star as France captain

fullText:
New France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane has confirmed his intention to continue with Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé as his captain moving forward.

Frontman Mbappé has for his part been in possession of the French captain's armband since all the way back in 2023, following the retirement of Hugo Lloris.

The honour was afforded to the 27-year-old by now-former Les Bleus headmaster Didier Deschamps.

Following Deschamps' exit in the aftermath of this summer's World Cup, though, it had been rumoured that the armband could head elsewhere, with many managers not in favour of their side being captained by a striker.

But for the aforementioned Zinedine Zidane, as much is evidently not considered an issue.

Speaking during an appearance in front of the media after naming his first-ever French squad on Friday evening, legendary midfielder 'Zizou' assured:

"Mbappé will be my captain. He's the best player in the world."

title: Francisco Roig highlights the biggest improvements Iga Swiatek has made this summer despite US Open disappointment
description: Iga Swiatek’s US Open campaign was brought to a halt in the fourth round with a surprising upset. The Pole came to New York in...
fullText:
Iga Swiatek's US Open campaign was brought to a halt in the fourth round with a surprising upset.

The Pole came to New York in fine form, having just captured her 12th WTA 1000 title at the Canadian Open before reaching the semifinals in Cincinnati.

Swiatek won each of her first three matches at the US Open in straight sets and looked to be a heavy favourite to reach the final.

But the six-time major champion fell to Qinwen Zheng in round four, with the Chinese star triumphing 7-5, 6-3.

A week and a half after her US Open exit, Swiatek's coach, Francisco Roig, pinpointed the biggest improvements the 25-year-old has made recently amid a topsy-turvy season.

"Above all, she made fewer mistakes," said Roig in an interview with Radio Zet, discussing Swiatek's last three tournament campaigns on the WTA Tour.

"The first rule in tennis is not to make them. I'm sure that when Iga wasn't advancing, she often lost. It wasn't like the other player was beating her. We were the ones losing.

"What does this mean? Iga made mistakes too often on her first serve. She tried too hard when she didn't need to.

"But Iga is Iga. She has to try. But in my opinion, sometimes she wants it too much. Opponents should be trying to play against her, and she doesn't have to do it every time. She needs to play more solidly. And in Toronto, she improved dramatically in this regard, and she also hit better quality balls.

"Her forehand had a better shape, and she played better angles on her backhand. This allowed her to extend each rally, and she later found easier balls to attack instead of trying to attack from more difficult positions.

"Fewer errors when serving high-quality balls yields a lot in tennis. With less effort, and without having to get to the ball so quickly. Sometimes Iga tries to get to the ball too quickly, and then she blocks her movement. We still need to improve all these things, and many more, but that's the foundation."

Swiatek is currently ranked ninth in the world, and she has lost 500 WTA points in the live rankings after not appearing at the Korea Open, which she won last year.

For the remainder of the season, Swiatek has just 335 WTA points to defend across two WTA 1000 tournaments: the China Open and the Wuhan Open.

Swiatek was knocked out in the fourth round of the China Open last year and reached the quarterfinals in Wuhan.

She will need to perform well during this year's Asian swing if she wants to play at the WTA Finals, which, as it stands, she is not set to qualify for.

Swiatek is currently 10th in the race to the WTA Finals. Only the top eight make the cut.

The last time Swiatek did not qualify for the prestigious year-end tournament was in 2019.

fullText:
Bulls news: Taj Gibson's bond with Derrick Rose goes way beyond basketball court appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

This week, Taj Gibson began his new role as an assistant coach for the Chicago Bulls. He played for the team for seven seasons in his 17-year career, where he made the biggest impact.

Along the way, Gibson played alongside Joakim Noah, Jimmy Butler, and especially Derrick Rose.

Speaking of Rose, Gibson has forged a tight bond with him that goes beyond the court, per Bulls on CHSN.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"That's my point guard…this is my family," Gibson said.

"That's my point guard…this is my family." 🤞

Taj Gibson on his bond with Derrick Rose ❤️ pic.twitter.com/gW6l12yYlM

— Bulls on CHSN (@CHSN_Bulls) September 17, 2026

It was in 2009, when the Bulls drafted Gibson, that things began to take a turn. The year before, Chicago drafted Rose with the No. 1 pick. At the time, the Bulls were trying to cultivate a new identity ten years after the dynasty run ended.

Meanwhile, Chicago was relegated to the NBA doldrums, losing season after season.

With Rose, Gibson, Noah, and eventually Butler among others, things began to turn around. In 2011, Rose won the NBA MVP, and the Bulls made it to the Eastern Conference Finals. Four years later, they made it to the Eastern Conference Semifinals.

In six out of Gibson's eight years in Chicago, they made the postseason. After Gibson announced his retirement, Rose paid tribute in a video featuring other Bulls players, teammates, and personnel.

Meanwhile, Gibson is getting a kick out of practice, learning from the new players amid a highly anticipated rebuilding season.

In January, Chicago retired Rose's jersey. Gibson celebrated Rose's legacy at the time.

Through all these years and so many changes, that bond remains unbreakable.

title: Eagles rule Jonathan Greenard out, list Andrew Mukuba as questionable
description: Jonathan Greenard is out and Andrew Mukuba is questionable, while Jalen Carter and Cooper DeJean have no status against Tennessee.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles will remain without one of their primary edge defenders when they travel to Nashville for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard has been ruled out because of a pectoral injury. Safety Andrew Mukuba is listed as questionable with a knee injury. Greenard was listed as a limited participant Friday, but the Eagles determined he was not ready to play.

His absence leaves Philadelphia relying on Nolan Smith Jr., Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa to generate pressure against Titans quarterback Cam Ward. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was dissatisfied with the pass rush after Philadelphia recorded one sack in its 24-22 victory over Washington. Greenard's continued absence places additional pressure on the available edge defenders to win their individual matchups while maintaining disciplined rush lanes against Ward.

Friday’s Injury Report#PHIvsTEN pic.twitter.com/gdkNrruSZ3

Mukuba was also listed as a limited participant Friday. His availability will be determined closer to kickoff. The second-year safety played every defensive snap against Washington alongside Cooper DeJean. Philadelphia received encouraging news involving DeJean and defensive tackle Jalen Carter.

Carter remained limited Friday because of a wrist injury, but he did not receive a game designation. DeJean practiced fully despite being listed with calf and abdomen injuries. Both are expected to be available against Tennessee.

Wide receivers Marquise Brown and Elijah Moore also practiced fully on Friday and carry no game designation. Brown had been listed with a hamstring injury, while Moore dealt with a neck issue.

description: There are a pair of all-local matchups that headline Week 2 action for SouthCoast football. Follow our scores throughout the night right here.

title: Florida State's defensive keys vs Alabama
description: Florida State needs a big performance from their defense against a capable Alabama offense. Here are their keys on that side of the ball.
fullText:
The Florida State Seminoles are in danger of starting the season 1-2 as they travel to face the No. 10 Alabama Crimson Tide this Saturday in Tuscaloosa. They're also on a nine-game losing streak on the road, which doesn't give a lot that of confidence that they can win this matchup.

For this upset to happen, FSU is going to need an inspired performance from its defensive unit. Through the first two games of the season, that side of the ball hasn't shown the consistency or growth that defenses under Tony White typically display in the second year under his watch.

Alabama's offense is capable of putting up a ton of points, and the game could get out of hand quickly if Florida State doesn't come to play. Here are five keys for the Seminoles' defense.

Russell has dual-threat capabilities, and letting him be effective in multiple areas will spell doom for FSU's defense. He will make plays, but the Seminoles can't afford to be on the field for long periods of time due to Russell moving the chains with his arm and his legs. They must keep him in the pocket as much as possible.

Hill is coming off his first 100-yard game against the Kentucky Wildcats. He has enough explosion to his game to be a very tough player to deal with, and if he's keeping the chains moving, Florida State will be vulnerable against the pass as things will open up. Stopping Hill should be a high priority for Tony White.

This has been an area of concern for FSU's defense this season so far. They've allowed a conversion rate of 58.1%, which is 135th in the FBS. Also, they have the worst EPA per play defensively in the nation at -1.33, and four of the five passing touchdowns they've surrendered have come on third down. They have to get off the field against Alabama.

This is an area that Florida State was expected to lean on in 2026. However, they haven't consistently gotten pressure on the quarterback, and SMU pushed them around for 155 yards rushing. In order for FSU to have a chance, guys like Daniel Lyons, Mandrell Desir, and Denante McCray must show up in a big way.

The Crimson Tide have been able to wear down their first two opponents by averaging over 35 minutes of possession time. It will be paramount for Florida State to end drives early, which speaks to being good on third down, which will keep Alabama in their own territory.

This was an area that FSU was supposed to lean on in 2026. However, the Seminoles haven't consistently gotten pressure on the quarterback, and against SMU, they were pushed around for 155 yards.

title: Oklahoma's OL faces underrated challenge against New Mexico
description: Oklahoma's offensive line needs to show improvement on Saturday against a top-ranked New Mexico defense.
fullText:
There is no question: if the Oklahoma Sooners want to make a run at another College Football Playoff berth, they need better play from their offensive line. The Sooners' offensive line struggled in the loss to Michigan, allowing 3.4 yards per carry and giving up three sacks and eight tackles for loss.

They now face a New Mexico Lobos team that ranks No. 3 in total defense, No. 16 in rushing yards allowed and is tied for No. 22 in sacks. While the Lobos will be outmatched from a size standpoint, they are very well coached and use tons of stunts and movement to cause disruption. They also play a similar style of defense to what the Michigan Wolverines played last weekend.

In that game, head coach Brent Venables revealed the performance was too uneven.

"They did some things that were really good," Venables said via Sooners Illustrated. "There were moments when we messed things up. We didn't block the right guy or target the right guy. Just the wrong fundamentals at the point of attack... When we got the numbers right with the safety 15 yards deep from the A gap, we left a zero technique unblocked, and they got us minus one in the second half when we needed to get a drive going... those are things you can't do. Those are some non-negotiables."

For an Oklahoma offense that already struggled to consistently sustain drives against Michigan, those details become even more important against New Mexico. The Sooners don't necessarily need a perfect performance from the offensive line, but they cannot afford repeated assignment errors that put the offense behind schedule.

With the Georgia Bulldogs waiting next week, Saturday gives the unit an immediate chance to prove the Michigan performance was a setback rather than a sign of a larger problem.

title: Celtics Fans Are Losing Their Minds Over Rookie's 49-Second Video
description: The viral offseason workout video strikes again.
fullText:
Celtics Fans Are Losing Their Minds Over Rookie's 49-Second Video originally appeared on NESN. 

Boston Celtics fans might be getting a little too excited about Chris Cenac Jr.

A 49-second clip of the Celtics rookie at a pickup game in New York City went viral this week. In it, Cenac was seen creating his own shot, knocking down some jumpers and running picture-perfect pick-and-rolls with Trae Young.

A post featuring Cenac's highlights has reached almost three million impressions on X.

7 footer moving like this ain’t normal man

Brad got the steal of the draft pic.twitter.com/BQJDi7Vp97

MORE: Luka Doncic's Lakers Sign Former Celtics Draft Pick

This is your reminder that the Celtics selected Cenac with the No. 27 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. Some analysts viewed the selection as a reach because of Cenac's raw skill set.

Cenac only played one season of college basketball at Houston. He started 36 of 37 games while averaging 9.5 points, 7.9 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 0.5 blocks. He wasn't the most efficient scorer, shooting 48.5 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from 3 as a freshman.

Still, Cenac has great size and a unique skill set for a 6-11 big man. Boston was drawn to that combination.

"He's just a good young player," Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens said. "Energetic, plays hard, excellent athlete, long. Fits a position of need, some things that we were a little short on this year from an athletic perspective, I think with his size and his length."

Late first-round picks aren't often expected to make an immediate impact, so you can't blame Celtics fans for getting excited to see Cenac look like he's ready to contribute from Day 1. Of course, workout videos can be highly misleading. Cenac also had the benefit of playing with Young, one of the NBA's best playmakers. He's made a career out of making bigs look good.

So, no, the video isn't proof that Boston found a steal at No. 27. But it's easy to understand why Celtics fans are excited to see Cenac flash the size, mobility and skill that made him such an intriguing prospect in the first place.

title: Report card: Bills defeat Lions in Week 2, 41-31
description: Grading the Bills in our report card following the team's 41-31 win over the Lions.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills clocked into work for the second time in the regular season during the 2026 NFL campaign and came out on top.

In Week 2, the Bills (2-0) took a rolled at home against the Detroit Lions (1-1) in a 41-31 win. It was a big win for the debut of the team's new home at Highmark Stadium.

Despite that, did the Bills earn high marks across the board for their effort?

With that, here are Bills Wire's Week 2 report card:

After a slower start in Week 1, running back James Cook played a big part for the Bills against the Lions. He had 135 yards on the ground, averaging 6.4 yards per carry with a touchdown. Detroit could not stop quarterback Josh Allen, either. He had two more scores.

Aside from the injury to wide receiver DJ Moore, nothing went wrong for the Bills in the air. Allen had three more scores in the air, including another improvisation play to receiver Josh Palmer on a play where he was simply a decoy down the middle of the field but ended up wide open down the middle.

The Bills scored touchdowns on their first four drives on offense. The Lions did not stand a chance after that.

Detroit leans heavily on running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Usually he's on an offense that can go back-and-forth with most, but they could not with the Bills. Because of that early scoring streak for Buffalo, the Bills' run defense was rarely tested.

The Lions tried to get Gibbs going and did see some momentum for one series, he couldn't. The Bills held Gibbs to just 52 yards rushing as he averaged only 3.3 yards per carry.

The Bills still struggle to cover receivers over the middle of the field. The Lions have one of the best wideouts out of the slot in Amon-Ra St. Brown and he had nine catches for 142 yards and two touchdowns. The pass rush had better spells against Detroit quarterback Jared Goff, but he did seem to find a rhythm eventually.

Sam Franklin committed a penalty on the opening kickoff, the first ever flag at Highmark Stadium. Coverage was not a problem otherwise.

Kicker Tyler Bass had a few blunders but converted otherwise. Bass missed an extra point and put his first kickoff into the end zone and giving the Lions 35 free yards.

Playing against his former team, punt returner Greg Dortch helped this grade. He had a 25-yard gainer.

title: Netflix Signs Andrés Cantor For Women's World Cup 2027 Coverage
description: After 26 years at Telemundo, the Emmy Award-winning broadcaster makes the move to the streaming platform, bringing his signature "¡GOOOOL!" call with him.
fullText:
Andrés Cantor is leaving Telemundo and heading to Netflix, bringing his ​s​ignature "¡GOOOOL!" with him.

Netflix announced ​today that the Argentin​e​ American, Emmy Award-winning broadcaster will join its broadcast team for the FIFA Women's World Cup 2027, ​​h​andling Spanish-language coverage​. The streamer, which acquired exclusive U.S. rights to the 2027 and 2031 tournament​s in 2024, named Cantor as its first play-by-play voice for the tournament​. The signing comes fresh off his coverage of the record-breaking men's World Cup on Telemundo this summer.

Netflix's choice to lead with Cantor​ speaks to his standing as one of the most recognized voices in Spanish-language sports broadcasting. Naming him first, ahead of any English-side talent, signals how much weight Netflix is putting on Spanish-speaking audiences as it builds its inaugural roster for the tournament.

​Cantor will begin his new role with the Final Draw on December 11, streaming live on Netflix across the United States and Canada from Rio de Janeiro's Museum of Modern Art.

"For more than four decades, I've had the privilege of sharing my love for soccer with audiences around the world, and I'm incredibly excited to continue that journey with Netflix ahead of a historic summer for the sport," Cantor sa​ys. "I've been fortunate to call some of the game's most unforgettable moments and create memories that I will always value. Now, as Netflix continues to expand its presence at the forefront of live sports, I'm thrilled to bring the FIFA Women's World Cup to fans across the United States and Canada and to capture the passion, emotion, and magnitude that make this tournament so special."

Cantor's voice has been a steady soccer soundtrack in the U.S. since the late 1980s, first on Univision and later on Telemundo.

A Hall of Fame broadcaster, Cantor's résumé spans men's and women's FIFA World Cups, the Summer Olympics, Copa América, the UEFA Champions League, the English Premier League, and Major League Soccer, among many other competitions worldwide.

​H​e has called every men's FIFA World Cup since 1986​, along with four Women's World Cup tournaments, including the inaugural competition in 1991. ​He covered the last three Women's tournaments for Telemundo, anchoring the network's onsite, in-venue announce team for the 2023 edition in Australia and New Zealand.

Before his 26 years at Telemundo, Cantor spent 13 years as a sports anchor at Univision.

Now he heads into his fifth Women's World Cup, and his first outside the Telemundo umbrella in ​m​ore than two decades.

His departure comes after his contract with the network ended, closing a run that made him the defining voice of Telemundo's FIFA World Cup coverage since the network picked up the U.S. Spanish-language rights from Univision in 2011.

"Andres has been an integral part of the Telemundo family helping bring audiences closer to the sport and playing a meaningful role in its remarkable growth across the country," Telemundo said in a statement. "We are grateful for everything he has contributed to Telemundo, our audiences and the game he loves. We thank him for his extraordinary legacy and wish him continued success in the next chapter of his career."

The Cantor signing builds on a deal Netflix struck back in 2024, when it secured exclusive U.S. rights to the Women's World Cup for both 2027 and 2031, the first time the tournament will live on a streaming platform.

Th​e​ deal covered the U.S., including Puerto Rico and ​Canada. Netflix's FIFA Women's World Cup coverage will air in English and Spanish in the United States, and in English and French in Canada.

It also ended a run for two legacy broadcasters. Telemundo had carried Spanish-language coverage of the Women's World Cup in the U.S. since 2015, while Fox Sports held the English-language rights across the 2015, 2019 and 2023 tournaments. FIFA's decision to unbundle men's and women's media rights for the first time opened the door for Netflix to grab both.

Netflix ​has been pushing for more live sporting events on its platform. At the time of the acquisition, Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria pointed to the streamer's boxing crossover as an early signal of appetite for women's sports, citing the Amanda Serrano-Katie Taylor fight as proof of concept before the FIFA deal closed.

Cantor's arrival is just the first talent piece Netflix has confirmed. The rest of its broadcast team will be announced closer to the tournament, which runs June 24 through July 25, 2027, across eight host cities in Brazil.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

fullText:
The spotlight may be on Lane Kiffin this week ahead of LSU's showdown with Ole Miss, but his son Knox had a game of his own to focus in on Thursday night.

With University Lab (LA) off to an 0-2 start, the Cubs needed a win to get their season back on track and Knox delivered on the road.

Knox completed 12 of his 15 passing attempts for 194 yards and four touchdowns while also rushing for 88 yards as the Cubs beat Plaquemine 31-21 for their first win of the season and first win over the Green Devils.

The win was a showcase for two sons of LSU's coaches as not only Kiffin shined, but Kevin Smith Jr., the son of LSU running backs coach Kevin Smith, caught all four of Kiffin's touchdown passes.

With the game and win out of the way, Knox and the rest of the Kiffin family can turn their attention back to Saturday night's massive matchup.

Not only will Saturday be a homecoming for Lane Kiffin as he'll coach against a Rebels squad he turned into a national powerhouse over the previous six seasons, but it will also be a homecoming for Knox Kiffin, who played for Oxford High School last season.

As a sophomore, Knox threw for 1,236 yards and accounted for 16 total touchdowns in eight games for a Chargers side that went on to finish the year 11-2 with their only two losses coming to Tupelo.

Once Saturday is out of the way, Knox Kiffin can turn his attention back to the remainder of the high school season. A 2028 three-star prospect, Knox and Cubs will return to action on Sept. 25 at home against Livonia as they look to extend their win streak to two games.

description:

fullText:
Though Europe has measures that address how consumers might encounter AI, technology will impact them if the worst scenarios bear

Europe’s dilemma over AI was rendered in stark terms this week. The head of the continent’s central bank, Christine Lagarde, said Europeans have two options: shun the technology and lose out on growth; or embrace it and become dependent on tools developed by the US and China.

The great debate over AI safety that has erupted in recent days threatens to make the choice moot. If the worst scenarios come to bear – and experts have differing views on this – then the technology will impact the continent regardless.

Europe has largely been absent from the highest levels of that debate, a result of the continent’s longstanding inability to produce a Silicon Valley-scale titan like Apple, Google or newcomer OpenAI. While it is a powerhouse in regulation, much to the White House’s chagrin, its lack of an Anthropic or Nvidia-sized frontrunner in the AI race has diminished its voice in the safety debate.

Ursula von der Leyen, a powerful political figure on the continent as president of the European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, addressed the issue this week by saying she will “invite the main frontier labs for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier”.

Her remarks gained nowhere as much traction as Donald Trump and China’s dismissal of a slowdown. Without the support of Washington or Beijing, any sort of pacing is impossible – with our without Europe’s input.

Lagarde’s speech on Monday underlined the continent’s relative weakness. She asserted that Europe must develop its own AI technology and build more datacentres in order to nullify the threat of being cut off by the US or China.

If Europe invests in its own AI tech, said Lagarde, “the threat of being cut off loses its force.” Self-sufficiency would also give Europe a chance to develop its own answer to the AI safety crisis.

Margrethe Vestager, who clashed with the US tech industry as the EU’s former competition commissioner, co-authored a report this week – A Transformative AI Strategy for Europe – that echoed Lagarde’s warning. AI threatens to accelerate a development already affecting Europe, where citizens “are already bearing the economic and social consequences of decisions taken elsewhere”, she says.

Solutions to this, according to the report, include building more datacentres – the central nervous systems of AI – and also to ensure the continent is resilient enough to withstand “AI crises” like a powerful model slipping out of control.

Vestager said that Europe does have a voice in the safety debate through its EU AI Act, the rare piece of AI legislation that sets out requirements for developers of “high-risk” AI systems to report safety incidents and address risks like a cutting-edge model evading control.

But she adds: “Europe must … build its own AI to strengthen the ecosystem, retain talent, and inspire innovation.”

Vestager acknowledges that if there is an existential threat, it requires a global solution; one that does not hand power to the US and China. And that requires a different kind of supranational body.

“As for existential threats to humanity, we must first assess the actual level of threat – then act with urgency. The UN general assembly is an opportunity to address this. It is vital to move beyond the US-China rivalry narrative. There must be space for humanity between the egos of leaders like President Xi and President Trump.”

Frederike Kaltheuner, an adviser to the AI Now Institute, a research body, says that Europe is dependent on US technology in ways that will be hard to undo, from search engines to chips to datacentres. But the narrative that Europe is grievously behind in the race depends on a particular view of artificial intelligence aggressively promoted by American tech bosses.

Because of their doomsday warnings, “we are exclusively talking about AI in a very narrow, specific kind of way – namely, the idea that there is such a thing as the AI frontier, which is getting better and better, and that access to the frontier is the most important thing that Europe needs for its security and economy.”

The reality of the market points at something else, she says: many companies are not adopting so-called “frontier models” – like ChatGPT and Anthropic – because of high costs and fears over what might happen to their data.

If this trend continues, Europe may not be so terribly positioned: the EU AI Act has a number of pragmatic measures which address how consumers might encounter AI on a day-to-day basis, legislating over matters such as labelling AI content, and the use of AI in medicine and hiring.

“Europe has a competitiveness problem, that’s true,” says Itxaso Dominguez de Olazabal, a policy adviser at EDRI, a European digital rights organisation. But US tech boosters are “blaming it on laws and protections, and have promised that deregulation will make European companies more competitive … in a race to the bottom to see if we can catch big tech”.

Nonetheless, the EU AI act is not viewed as model legislation for other countries or a vehicle for a global slowdown. Georgina Kon, a partner at law firm Linklaters, says the act is unlikely to be adopted as a global benchmark for several reasons, including criticisms of the heavy compliance burden, which has led to delays in parts of the act becoming active, and a narrow territorial focus on Europe. Those criticisms have also meant that lawmakers elsewhere have looked to differentiate their approach to AI legislation from the EU’s. 

 “The EU AI Act is not something that everybody else in the world feels constrained by, although many tech companies will of course want to sell to the EU,” she says.

Big tech still has a vast customer base in Europe. Kaltheuner worries that the doomsday narratives will push Europe towards dependency, encouraging it to adopt US AI models across the economy out of ill-defined fears over being left behind.

“There’s a vision of the future where Europe’s economy, its public sector, its education system runs on models and on infrastructure that is controlled by a very small number of companies that happen to be also in the US. This would be a sovereignty problem.”
