If You Loved 'Outlander,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next
description: If “Outlander” was your ideal time-travel romance, here’s a movie you should really check out.
fullText:
Outlander filled a void no one suspected existed (probably). Based on the bestselling book series by Diana Gabaldon, this epic love story about a time-traveling woman who plunges into the messiest extramarital affair ever known was one of the most popular shows on TV screens, and inspired some intense fandom. If you were one of the show’s superfans and you’re not quite sure how to fill your time now that Claire and Jamie’s story is done, there’s some good news: The best movie for Outlander fans to watch was released decades ago, in 1980.

Based on the 1975 novel Bid Time Return by Richard Matheson, Somewhere in Time is one of those movies that people still talk about almost fifty years after its release—and it’s a spookily perfect companion to Outlander.

Christopher Reeve, fresh off his star turn in Superman, plays playwright Richard Collier. While on a road trip, he stops at the Grand Hotel and sees a photo of Elise McKenna (Jane Seymour), who was a famous actress in the early 20th century. He realizes that an elderly Elise had given him an antique pocket watch years earlier, and comes to believe that time travel is possible and begins planning for a trip back to 1912—succeeding after several tries.

In the past, he meets Elise, and they fall madly in love—but her manager sees Richard as a threat to her career, and does everything he can to thwart them. It’s a story that parallels Outlander’s in many ways, especially when Claire decides to return to the 18th century to seek Jamie after she learns that he’s still alive. Richard’s determination to stay with Elise no matter what ends up in tragedy (something else fans of Outlander are familiar with), but the story asks a simple question: Isn’t suffering worth it if it leads you to true love?

Somewhere in Time doesn’t get to dig as deeply into Richard and Elise’s love story as Outlander does with Jamie and Claire, of course—the series was able to linger on their story over more than 100 episodes. But the film captures the same powerful moment of connection as two people overcome the most fundamental obstacle in the universe—time—in order to be together. Fans of the show will love it. Stream Somewhere in Time on The Roku Channel, Tubi, or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Iif you still need more timeless time-travel romance in your life, there are more movies to check out.

Frothier, funnier, and sillier than Outlander or Somewhere in Time, Kate & Leopold is the story of Leopold, the impoverished Duke of Albany (Hugh Jackman). Living in New York City in 1876, he is on the verge of inventing the Otis elevator when he chases a man through a time portal and finds himself in 2001. There’s a lot of plot about elevators and temporal paradoxes, but Outlander fans will come for the romance Leopold falls into with the man’s ex, Kate McKay (Meg Ryan). The thoroughly modern Kate is wooed by Leopold’s old-fashioned charm and intelligence, and it leads to one of those classic romcom moments where someone has to race to be with their soulmate, except instead of a plane they’re racing toward a time portal, as one does. Rent Kate & Leopold on Prime Video.

Another film adapted from a novel (Second Sight by David L. Williams), The Two Worlds of Jennie Logan stars Lindsay Wagner as Jennie, a woman who moves into an old Victorian house with her estranged husband, who has confessed to an affair. Legends about the house center on a previous owner, David (Marc Singer), who claimed to see the ghost of his dead wife and supposedly died in a duel. When Jennie finds an old dress hanging in a closet and tries it on, she finds herself transported to 1899 several times. When she finally meets David, she realizes she was the “ghost” he spoke of. They fall in love, but a jealous rival threatens everything in this surprisingly twisty movie that Outlander fans will appreciate. Stream The Two Worlds of Jennie Logan on The Roku Channel or YouTube.

One of the most effective aspects of Outlander is how it explores the necessity of leaving something behind in order to truly appreciate it. In Peggy Sue Got Married, Peggy Sue (Kathleen Turner) is recently separated from her philandering husband, Charlie (Nicholas Cage). When she’s transported from 1986 back to her senior year of high school in 1960 and given a chance to change the entire course of her life, she has to wrestle with what could have been versus what she still might have in the “real” present. It’s got plenty of funny moments, but Peggy Sue Got Married is, at its core, a love story. Stream Peggy Sue Got Married on Tubi or rent it on Prime Video.

Whether there is any actual time travel or immortality in this complex, symbolically rich film is debatable—writer/director Darren Aronofsky left much of the story open to interpretation. But it’s 100% a love story that spans centuries in one sense or another, as Hugh Jackman plays three versions of a man named Tom (or Tomás, as he is called when he is a Spanish Conquistador in the 16th century). In the present day, Dr. Tom Creo searches for a cure for death as his beloved wife, Izzi, dies of a brain tumor. And in the far future, Tom travels through space with what may be the Tree of Life, seeking to be reunited with Izzi in some way. It’s lushly romantic whether you choose to believe that all the Toms are real or that some of them are imaginary, and a deeply affecting story fans of the show will love. Rent The Fountain on Prime Video.

Timeline, based on the book by Michael Crichton, isn’t a love story—but if your favorite part of Outlander is the fish-out-of-water aspect of a person from the future finding their way in the past, this is the perfect choice. When a group of archaeology grad students is sent back to 1357 to discover the fate of their professor, everything that can go wrong quickly does, stranding them in the midst of The Hundred Years’ War between the English and the French. The film presents the challenges of adapting to the past in a relatively realistic way, and the twists and turns of its fast-paced plot are a lot of fun. There’s a romance in there, too, though it’s far from the focus—but if you’re looking for more grand adventure via the magic of time travel, this movie is a treat. Rent Timeline on Prime Video.

title: Do the Apple Watch Series 12's New Health Features Live Up to the Hype?
description: I have the newest Apple Watch in my hands, and I've already begun putting its newest features to the test.
fullText:
I now have the Apple Watch Series 12 in my hands—or, rather, on my wrist—and have spent the past 24 hours putting it through as many tests as I can manage. I'm pleased with the step counting and the availability of "recovery HRV" (as opposed to the cardiac-health-focused HRV that the Apple Watch previously used) but I'm not sure if the heart rate accuracy is living up to the hype. I'll be putting this device to more rigorous tests, but here are my first thoughts.

Apple waited forever to add step counting as an easily viewable metric on the watch, but it’s finally here. I can open my smart stack (with a double pinch of my fingers, not even touching the watch screen) and see my steps right on top. I’ve also added a step count complication to my watch face. You can find this complication under Activity. The option to see your rings as a complication is still there, but you can now also add steps or wheelchair pushes.

Step counts work well. They update quickly, and seem to be accurate in my casual counting—nine steps from my desk to the door registers as nine steps. I’ll do more in-depth testing soon, to properly evaluate Apple’s claim that it now has the most accurate step counting out there.

What’s disappointing is that it took so long—and that step counting is not coming to the Series 11 or any earlier watch. Apple’s step counting uses a special pedometer model that’s built into its new processor. Older Apple watches don’t have the hardware to calculate your steps as precisely, leading Apple to leave the feature off those watches. That is wild to me, considering that every other wearable has had step counts on the watch ever since the first cave dweller strapped a rock to their wrist.

Apple claims the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate in a wearable, and I’ve already mentioned that that's a bold claim given what I’ve seen in the past from Apple and from other devices. Now that I have a Series 12 in my hands, I was able to do some preliminary testing.

To be totally clear, these are not thorough tests, and I’m not making a decisive conclusion based on just a few days’ testing. But I’ll show you what I’ve tried so far.

As always, I’m testing the device against my heart rate as read by a chest strap (the gold standard for heart rate comparisons). I did:

A treadmill interval run with the Series 11 and a chest strap

An identical treadmill interval run with the Series 12, a chest strap, and the Garmin Forerunner 570 for good measure

An outdoor run that included steady jogging, intervals, and walking, with the Series 12, a chest strap, and the 570.

I’m including the 570 in these tests because it has what I would consider the most accurate heart rate sensor in a wearable. In my past testing it’s reported numbers that were identical or nearly identical to the chest strap. That said, there’s always variation from day to day, and it didn’t shine quite as well in these recent tests compared to some I’ve done in the past.

Here are the indoor runs with the Series 11 on top, and the Series 12 on the bottom, both in red and both compared to a chest strap. The Series 11 was already doing a pretty good job, and to be honest I’m not sure if the Series 12 is any better. I’m disappointed that the Series 12 is still only sampling heart rate every five seconds during workouts. Other devices, like the chest strap and the Garmin, sample every second. That means Apple is taking 12 data points every minute while these other devices are taking 60.

Here’s the outdoor run. The chest strap is in gray, Garmin in blue, and Apple in red. Again, the sparse data points of the Apple watch aren’t impressive. I see a few places where Apple missed the peak of a small spike, but then again the Garmin struggled in a few spots as well. I’ll do further testing and report back when I’ve been able to try out the watch in a greater variety of activities and conditions.

Live Rewind and Siri Recaps aren’t available yet. Live Rewind is the feature where you can ask for a text transcription of whatever was said around you in the last 15 seconds. Recaps handle a longer timeframe—for example, to summarize a meeting. These features are coming later this year, and aren’t in the version of watchOS 27 that came with the watch. (I have not installed any beta software on the watch.)

Readiness is another big feature coming soon, but I haven’t logged enough nights of sleep to get my scores yet—it needs about a week of data. As a preview, I am seeing my “recovery HRV” listed with my sleep data. Last night my HRV was 45 according to Apple, and 50 according to my Oura ring. HRV readings from different devices may vary, depending on exactly when they take their measurements, so I’ll be looking for trends rather than specific data points. If both devices agree on what is a high or a low reading for me, given my baseline, I’ll call that a success for Apple.

title: The Best Home Entertainment Gifts for Every Type of Person
description: Find the perfect home entertainment gift for everyone on your gift list.
fullText:
If you're planning on giving home entertainment gear as a gift this holiday, forget about traditional benchmarks like "biggest screen" or "most expensive speakers." Match the gear with the personality and needs of the person being entertained by that home entertainment system instead. Below are my best picks for everyone from college kids squeezed in a dorm room to legacy media snobs for whom streaming video isn't an option.

You probably won't buy someone a new TV for the holidays, but you can give the media-hound on your list a gadget to make the TV they already own even better. Enhancing watching and gaming is the mission of the Philips Hue Play Sync Box. It’s a middleman between TVs and HDMI gear like consoles or streaming boxes that analyzes video signals in real time and tells the connected smart light strip (as well as other compatible smart lights) to match what's on screen. This is great for gaming immersion, but it also improves just watching TV. Projecting colors behind the set that complement the visuals gives the illusion of a bigger screen, and it's just cool.

The Magnetar UDP800 isn't for casual media consumers, but if you're giving a present to the type of person who sneers at streaming and demands picture and sound at the highest possible quality, consider a Magnetar. This thing is monster. Magnetar laughs at the compression of Netflix by reading 4K video at bitrates up to 100 Mbp. It humiliates Spotify with lossless audio in formats like Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD Master Audio. It's also a true universal player, handling everything from 4K UHD Blu-rays and standard DVDs to Kodak Picture CDs. Like the best niche gear, it's expensive, but I'm sure your purist is worth the cost.

Most take it as a given that a huge, semi-matte black rectangle will dominate every living room like the monolith from 2001, but some people don't buy into it. If there's someone like that on your list, the Anker Nebula Cosmos 4K projector is the perfect gift. It's small enough that they can put it in a closet to keep their decor pure and pretend they don't even know what a television is, and it still projects a crisp, 4K image on any flat wall so they can watch Love Island in high def when everyone else is asleep. The portability makes it perfect for a backyard film festival too.

If there's a college student who plays video games on your Secret Santa list (and every college student plays video games), send them back to the dorms with a ROG Xbox Ally X20. This versatile system functions as a portable game system for killing time between classes with either PC or Xbox games. It hooks right up to a cheap dorm TV for late-night gaming sessions, and it runs a full version of Windows 11 for actually doing work.

It's wild that there is a class of audio equipment designed for people to not listen to, but these earbuds solve a real problem, particularly for anyone with young children. Soundcore Sleep A20 Earbuds contain a noise-masking system designed to block out any unwanted sounds and improve your sleep. They're designed with the ergonomic needs of sleepers in mind, and they even track your "sleeping analytics" so you can make sure your slumber is up-to-par. If your giftee would rather not collapse into dreamless sleep through white noise, these can be used as normal Bluetooth earbuds too.

You ever see the movie All that Heaven Allows? Jane Wyman plays a widow who starts dating a much younger man, but her children don't approve of the soulful lumberjack, so they wreck their relationship, then give her a TV so she doesn't get lonely in her tomb of a home. You will not be creating the same energy by giving the empty nesters on your list a Samsung 95H: That lumberjack was sort of creepy, and having an empty nest is cool, actually. An ultra-thin, 77-inch 4K OLED TV is better than human connections anyway: This is a really nice television. The design is tasteful—thin metallic frame, matte display surface—and the picture is about as good as you can get in 2026.

title: North Korean anthem played for South Korea at Asian Games
description: Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.
fullText:
Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.

South Korea, who thrashed Bangladesh 5-0, looked confused as the incorrect national anthem was played.

South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported that Bangladesh's national anthem followed before South Korea's actual anthem was played.

A stadium announcer did apologise for the mistake.

"This is a really serious problem. When we protested, they said, 'We're sorry. It wasn't that it wasn't prepared; there was a mistake on the part of those responsible for playing it'," South Korea coach Min Tae-seok said.

"But this is something that simply should never happen."

North Korea's national anthem, along with other symbols of the secretive state, are banned in South Korea.

The two countries are still technically at war, after the 1950-53 conflict between the two ended without a peace treaty.

The build-up to the Asian Games, which officially starts on Saturday, has already seen complaints from teams about the quality and amount of accommodation.

A member of the South Korea basketball team posted a video of a leaking pipe and soaked floor in his room, with the caption: "Please help me."

Some teams were also stranded at the airport for up to six hours when they landed this week.

Field hockey at the Asian Games started on Friday and runs until 3 October.

title: Hedges pays tribute to late trainer Hatton at weigh-in
description: John Hedges pays tribute Ricky Hatton by wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with images of his late trainer as he weighs in for Saturday's fight with Pat Brown in Manchester.
fullText:
John Hedges paid tribute to Ricky Hatton by wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with images of his late trainer as he weighed in for Saturday's fight with Pat Brown in Manchester.

Hatton, a two-weight world champion, was found dead at his Manchester home in September 2025, aged 46.

The 'Hitman' moved into coaching after retiring in 2012 and Hedges spent time working under Hatton and had him in his corner when he won the English cruiserweight title in May 2025.

Essex's Hedges, 24, was booed during the weigh-in at Manchester's New Century Hall, with the majority of those in attendance showing support for local fighter Brown.

But Hedges, who pointed to the images of Hatton on his T-shirt, insisted he was unfazed by the reaction.

"This isn't a hostile atmosphere, this is second nature to me," he said. "I've boxed at a high level as an amateur and this is what you get used to.

"Pat knows the crack, he knows where I've been and this is nothing new. I'm blessed to be here but this is nothing new."

Hedges has yet to lose in 12 professional fights and faces Brown - who has a won all six of his fights by knockout - for the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles.

Saturday's contest was initially due to take place at Planet Ice in Altrincham, but had to be upgraded to the much larger Co-op Live arena due to demand for tickets.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn told IFL TV earlier this week he expected a crowd of around 5,000 at the event.

Brown, who represented Team GB at the 2024 Olympics, has a growing fanbase in his home city and was greeted by chants of, 'Oh, Patrick the Bomber', in reference to his nickname.

He has looked relaxed during previous media activities during the week but was very intense when he spoke after both fighters tipped the scales at 14st 3lb (90kg).

"This is what I was born to do," Brown said.

"Since I was seven years old and my dad took me into the gym - this is what I was born to do."

title: 'Living legend' Gray advanced Hibs, says Newell
description: Club captain Joe Newell insists sacked head coach David Gray can be proud of his record at Hibernian and believes his replacement has plenty of time to deliver success this season.
fullText:
Club captain Joe Newell insists sacked head coach David Gray can be proud of his record at Hibernian and believes his replacement has plenty of time to deliver success this season.

Gray's 12-year stay at Easter Road came to an end on Wednesday, with Hibs on a run of three successive Scottish Premiership defeats and ninth in the table after six games.

"It's been a tough week for everyone," said 33-year-old midfielder Newell, who was a team-mate of Gray's when he signed in 2019 and who was made skipper when the former boss took charge.

"There's an element of blame for all of us. He always took responsibility, always protected his players, which I thought was noble and kind of summed him up as a man.

"Football moves on quickly, but I think it's important everyone at the club remembers him for what he's done - and I'm sure they will. He's not just a living legend. He'll go down in history."

Gray captained Hibs to Scottish Cup glory in 2016, famously scoring a stoppage-time winner against Rangers in the final at Hampden.

As a rookie head coach, he led the Edinburgh side to third and fifth-place finishes.

"His time in charge of the club was a massive success," Newell said. "The more time goes on, the more people will appreciate that.

"From the place we were in to where we went under Dave is something he should be proud of.

"We've had some amazing memories over the last couple of years and some really good achievements."

Painful endgame for Gray as stale Hibs slump

Gray sacked by Hibs after six league games

Hibs face Aberdeen on Saturday hoping to avoid what would be a club record of seven successive home league defeats.

"The main thing is the reaction, to try and get back on winning terms with a performance the fans can get behind," Newell said.

Hibs will meet city rivals Heart of Midlothian in the Premier Sports Cup semi-finals on 1 November and Newell is sure this campaign can be a fruitful one.

"All we can do as players is buy into whoever is in charge," he added.

"There's no crisis in terms of saving the season. It's still early on. We are in a position where we can turn it round quickly.

"I've said it a few times on record that this squad, and especially over the last 12 months, is the best squad I've been involved in, so I'm massively confident that we can still achieve what we've set out to achieve."

title: Sheeraz withdraws from next bout & gives up WBO title
description: Hamzah Sheeraz has withdrawn from a proposed bout with Janibek Alimkhanuly and relinquished his WBO super-middleweight title, the sanctioning body has confirmed.
fullText:
Hamzah Sheeraz has withdrawn from a proposed bout with Janibek Alimkhanuly and relinquished his WBO super-middleweight title, the sanctioning body has confirmed.

The British fighter was mandated by the organisation to face the Kazakhstan boxer, who is the WBO's number one challenger for the title.

A purse bid was held on Thursday for the right to host the bout, which Sheeraz's promoters Queensberry won with a bid of $1,001,809 (£747,903). Top Rank were the only other bidders, but fell short with their $850,000 (£634, 569) offer.

The British promoters had planned to stage the bout on either 28 November or 5 December with London, Birmingham and New York proposed locations.

But the WBO confirmed on Friday night Sheeraz, 27, had withdrawn from the bout.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri posted on X: "The WBO confirms that Queensberry Promotions has formally notified in writing that Hamzah Sheeraz, per the terms resulting from the purse bid proceedings concerning his mandatory obligation against Janibek Alimkhanuly, has elected not to proceed with the mandatory and has voluntarily relinquished his WBO super-middleweight world championship.

"The WBO acknowledges and respects the decision of Hamzah and his team.

"The WBO doors will always remain open to him, and we sincerely wish Hamzah and his team all the very best and continued success moving forward.

"The WBO World Championship Committee will render the applicable ruling on Monday, September 21, regarding the status of the WBO super-middleweight world championship and the division moving forward."

Sheeraz's manager Spencer Brown has been contacted for comment.

Alimkhanuly's manager Egis Klimas claimed on X earlier on Friday that Sheeraz had withdrawn from the bout.

He posted: "Ha, I was right, if you scared yesterday, you scared today and you will be scared tomorrow. Couple things you can't train in boxing, chin and scariness. Been informed Hamzah Sheeraz has vacated WBO title. What ashamed! [sic]"

Sheeraz, who has a record of 24 wins and one draw, won the super-middleweight title when he beat Alem Begic in May, before defending it against Simon Zachenhuber in July.

Alimkhanuly's position for the title has been controversial. Last December, just before a defence of the WBO and IBF middleweight titles, the 33-year-old returned a positive test for meldonium.

He was suspended for a year by the WBO in February but they allowed him to retain their title, while the IBF stripped him of theirs.

However, in July the WBO terminated his suspension early and installed Alimkhanuly as mandatory challenger at super-middleweight for Sheeraz's title.

"I think it's a joke. I think what the WBO has done here is disgraceful to the sport of boxing as well," Sheeraz told The Ariel Helwani Show in August.

title: Uefa & Concacaf demand Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members
description: Uefa and Concacaf issue a joint statement calling on Fifa to pay $10m from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.
fullText:
Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino calling on Fifa to pay at least $10m (£7.5m) from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.

It is the latest chapter in the war of words between the governing bodies, in response to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's aborted private equity proposal.

Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to an investment company.

The idea was scrapped after four days following widespread opposition from national associations.

The letter, seen by BBC Sport, was signed by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin and his Concacaf counterpart Victor Montagliani.

It outlines that "Fifa is on course to close 2023-26 with reserves of approximately $6bn (£4.5bn)" which is "considerably more than is required" through to the 2030 men's World Cup.

It said that Fifa should "make at least $10m available to each of its 211 member associations over the 2027-30 cycle" which should be used "for investment in infrastructure and football development".

This "one-off release of reserves" would come at a cost of $2.11bn (£1.57bn), and would be in addition to the regular funding in the cycle.

When the controversial plan was revealed in the days following the World Cup final, Infantino told members they would receive $40m (£30m) if they backed it.

Infantino set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (£15m).

In the letter, Ceferin and Montagliani said analysis carried out on Fifa's published financial statements and budgets raised doubts that the FFE proposal was "necessary to deliver greater resources".

It added that the analysis was "deliberately conservative" and a larger distribution from the reserves should be considered by the Fifa Council once the financial position at year-end is known.

An "independent review" of Fifa's finances should be commissioned, it added, with "full access to the underlying figures and assumptions".

"Fifa currently holds billions of dollars in accumulated reserves," it read. "These resources belong to football and exist to serve the game and its 211 member associations.

"Prudence should not prevent a careful examination of whether a portion could responsibly be released to the extent those reserves exceed Fifa's foreseeable needs.

"Releasing part of these reserves would demonstrate that member associations should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits.

"Development is an institutional responsibility of Fifa – not a matter of individual discretion."

Another letter, also seen by BBC Sport, has been sent to the presidents of the other confederations - Asia, Africa, South America and Oceania - asking them to support the motion.

The news comes a day after Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt sent a letter to Infantino and Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom demanding that all documents relating to the controversial FFE plan were released.

Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, said that the Fifa Council should also receive a written explanation for the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup.

Infantino was told he should make all documents available before the next Fifa Council meeting, which is on 15 October.

Infantino, 56, will stand for election for a fourth time in March, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

title: Uefa rejected request to keep Republic of Ireland and Israel separate - FAI
description: The Football Association of Ireland says it had a request to keep the Republic of Ireland and Israel separate in future competition draws rejected by Uefa.
fullText:
Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell says it had a request to keep the Republic of Ireland and Israel separate in future competition draws rejected by Uefa.

After being grouped together in February's draw, the Republic of Ireland and Israel are set to meet in Nations League fixtures on 27 September and 4 October.

In June, the FAI confirmed its home game on 4 October would be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia, as opposed to Dublin's Aviva Stadium, while no tickets will be made available for Irish fans for Israel's 'home' fixture in Debrecen, Hungary.

At an extraordinary general meeting in July, delegates backed an FAI motion to proceed with the games amid concerns that boycotting would cause "significant and lasting harm" for the association.

However, the decision to fulfil the fixtures has come under increasing pressure amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, with a 'Stop The Game' campaign launched by Irish Sport for Palestine calling for a boycott.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Courell said European football's governing body Uefa rejected the association's request about future draws, which was made after the teams were drawn together in February.

"The response was pretty clear. They [Uefa] have a formal term for it, I can't remember the formal term, the 'do not draw' list or whatever. It's based, really, on conflicts, direct conflicts, not public sentiment," said, external Courell.

"The answer I got was very clear. That would not be possible, because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict. That was an answer that I took at face value."

BBC Sport NI has contacted Uefa for comment.

Israel fixtures an 'uncomfortable situation' for FAI

The 'Stop the Game' campaign has received support from former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr and ex-player James McClean, and May's friendly against Qatar in Dublin was disrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch.

Speaking to RTE, Courell said he "appreciated" the "strength of sentiment" among the Irish public regarding the games and pointing out that the FAI previously called on Uefa to ban Israel from European competition.

"We wish we weren't in this position. We have publicly called for, and formally called for, Israel's removal from international football," he said.

"We were the only federation in Uefa, so one out of 55 that has done so formally. But at an institutional level, that hasn't happened yet.

"As such, the decision rested with the FAI and we wanted particularly now to offer our spport and protection to the players because it's a decision that rested with the FAI board."

He added: "We have spoken to Uefa extensively over the last year, yes. And their response? It's the same as it has been for some time. They recognise the strength of conviction from the FAI on this topic and how that reflects the solidarity the Irish people have of the Palestinian plight.

"But equally they have to consider the sentiment of 54 other nations. And unfortunately, at this moment in time, it's not universal."

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza. The United Nations believes the retaliation has killed more than 70,000 Palestinians.

Israel has regularly denied committing genocide or war crimes and has said its actions in Gaza have been justified as a means of self-defence.

title: Northampton agree deal with Pato-led consortium
description: Northampton reach agreement with a consortium including former Brazil forward Alexandre Pato over a "proposed shareholding acquisition".
fullText:
Northampton Town have confirmed they have reached agreement with a consortium including former AC Milan, Chelsea and Brazil forward Alexandre Pato over a "proposed shareholding acquisition" in the League Two club.

Sports Alpha Capital (SAC) had their proposed deal with the Cobblers approved by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and English Football League (EFL) earlier this month.

In a statement, the club said they expected to be "in a position to confirm completion of the process" next week.

"Football club transactions always have many moving parts and often take a little longer than you would hope, but we are thrilled to be moving forward," said Northampton chairman Kelvin Thomas.

Joao Xavier, founding partner at Sports Alpha Capital, added: "We are very happy to have reached formal agreements.

"Obviously obtaining IFR and EFL approvals was a big step, but this is also a very important milestone, and we look forward to closing next week."

Sports Alpha Capital (SAC) had been in discussions about taking over Colchester United earlier this year but decided to pull out of a potential deal following initial talks.

Pato is named by SAC, external as one of its investors, along with Gemcorp Capital, a London-based independent investment management firm.

The size of SAC's proposed shareholding in the Cobblers has not been disclosed at this stage.

Pato, 37, retired from playing last year. He is best known for his five-and-a-half-year spell at AC Milan where he scored 63 goals in 150 matches and won the Serie A title in the 2010-11 season.

The Cobblers suffered relegation to the fourth tier last season, finishing bottom of League One.

They are currently 17th in League Two after winning for the first time this season when they beat Newport at home on 5 September.

In April, the club announced a pre-tax loss just short of £3m, with Thomas previously saying the proposed investment would make the club debt-free.

BMW PGA Championship - round two

Selected others: -8 R Fox (NZ), R Fisher (Eng), R McIlroy (NI), I Elvira (Spa), JJ Spaun (US); -7 M Wallace (Eng); -6 S Straka (Aut), A Noren (Swe); -5 L Aberg (Swe), V Hovland (Nor); -4 D Law (Sco), R MacIntyre (Sco), S Lowry (Ire), M Fitzpatrick (Eng); -3 J Rose (Eng)

Rory McIlroy stayed in contention with a five-under 67 to sit four strokes behind second-round leader Ryan Gerard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

The Northern Irishman made three birdies in his opening five holes and recovered from dropped shots on the eighth and 16th by picking up four strokes on the back nine, including birdies on the 17th and 18th holes.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy's hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title were also buoyed by the withdrawal of Patrick Reed after nine holes.

The American, who currently leads the standings on the DP World Tour, had been well placed after the first round but was forced to retire through injury while nine-over par for Friday's round.

"Unfortunately he's pulled out this week, which gives me an opportunity to try to claw back some ground that I lost last week in Ireland," said McIlroy, who is at eight under overall.

"This weekend is a big weekend for me to pick up a few points and make the race even tighter going into these last few weeks. I'm in a great spot heading into the weekend."

Gerard made five birdies and an eagle in a flawless round of 65 to leave him two shots clear of Australia's Adam Scott and Italian Filippo Celli, who are at 10 under.

US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, who played alongside McIlroy and Open champion Ryan Fox in a marquee group, also enjoyed a birdie-birdie finish as he signed for a 69.

The Englishman, who had shared the lead overnight, was at nine under alongside Spain's Manuel Elvira, with McIlroy and Fox among a quintet of players a further shot back.

Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka was among the big names to miss the cut at one over.

Englishman Tommy Fleetwood will also miss the weekend after a 74 left him at three over, while Spain's Jon Rahm endured another day to forget, following up a six-over-par 78 on Thursday with a 77 to end 138th and last of all those to finish on Friday.

York Valkyrie will meet reigning Women's Super League champions Wigan Warriors in the Grand Final after beating Leeds Rhinos at AMT Headingley Stadium.

Leon Pryce's team, who last week ended Wigan's 100 per cent record to book their place in the semi-final, managed tries through forwards Liv Wood and Adaoha Akwiwu in a tight contest.

Leeds had inflicted heavy defeats on their opponents in the two regular season meetings at home, but they went into the match on the back of four straight losses, and their lack of confidence showed as they came up with errors at vital moments.

The only downside for York was that their influential stand-off Tara-Jane Stanley will miss the September 27 meeting with Wigan at the Brick Community Stadium after failing a head injury assessment.

That will be a serious blow for York, who beat Wigan 26-12 last week, and a personal blow for Stanley, whose return from a two-year injury absence had sparked their run of four wins in their past five games.

They were on the front foot for most of the game and deservedly went ahead when pressure on the Rhinos line ended with England prop Liv Wood forcing her way over despite the attentions of three tacklers.

Stanley's kicking game was important in the success, and she added the conversion and kicked a penalty to give her side breathing space at half-time.

Leeds rallied in the second half and, after Stanley had a try disallowed for a knock-on and Megan Pakulis was denied a try by a brilliant Ruby Bruce tackle, the Rhinos seemed to have struck back only for Georgia Elliston's try to be disallowed for obstruction by a team-mate.

Stanley came up with the telling moment, a lovely pass to send Akwiwu over for York's second try, and when Ebony Stead fumbled as she went to touch down, the home side's hopes of a late revival were over.

title: Carse assault investigation dropped by police
description: England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further police action after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month is dropped.
fullText:
England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further action from the police after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month was dropped.

Footage of Carse appeared on social media, showing him in handcuffs and surrounded by police on Sunday, 23 August. The footage was captured in the early hours of that day.

It emerged that the 31-year-old had been arrested and then de-arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly.

Later that week, after Carse had been removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan, Derbyshire Police confirmed it was looking at allegations of assault.

In a statement released on Friday, the police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in The Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday, 23 August.

"A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

Carse will now be subject to an investigation from the Cricket Regulator. The Regulator has not commented. The England and Wales Cricket Board and Carse have both been approached for comment.

The incident in Derby was the latest in a string of late-night alcohol-related controversies to hit the England men's team in the past year.

After Carse was dropped from the second Test against Pakistan, Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and revealed he had addressed his team to make his feelings clear.

Though Carse has continued to be play for his county Durham, he was also left out of the England squads for the third Test against Pakistan and the white-ball series with Sri Lanka.

After he was omitted from the games against Sri Lanka, the ECB confirmed that Carse is available for selection.

"Whilst Brydon was available for selection, he has not been picked for the Sri Lanka series squad," said an ECB statement. "Given recent events, we feel it is important for him to work through the issues that led to the Derby incident and take time for a proper reset.

"This decision does not prejudge the outcome of any investigation."

Earlier this week, England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum said Carse needs to "get his house in order" before returning to international cricket.

Carse did not play in Durham's game against Worcestershire this week. The county said he was "unwell".

title: London City's new training centre 'better than most Premier League clubs' - Kang
description: Michele Kang believes London City Lionesses' planned new training ground will set a new standard in the women's game and surpass facilities used by most men's Premier League clubs.
fullText:
Michele Kang believes London City Lionesses' planned training ground will set a new standard in the women's game and surpass facilities used by the majority of men's Premier League clubs.

Over the summer, Kang boosted the Women's Super League side with significant investment in players, including the signing of two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Kang revealed a purpose-built training centre is expected to open within the next year.

She said: "We're building a state-of-the-art training centre for our female athletes dedicated to them, built and designed for them, which will open in less than a year.

"Our architect, who has built several Premier League training centres told me that by the time the London City training centre is up and running, it would be better than with the majority of Premier League men's teams training centres."

Kang views investment in infrastructure as part of a wider remit to ensure female athletes are no longer treated differently from their male counterparts.

"How could you possibly accept the notion that your girls, your daughters, granddaughters, sisters are treated as second-class citizens where in the same sport the boys go to play as if it's their birthright?"

She believes that for too long, women have been treated like "small men".

"We have to take care of our female players better so that they can train, perform, and thrive as female athletes, not small men," she said.

"You drive your boy to a state-of-the-art training centre and then, if you're lucky enough to have a facility nearby, you drive your girl somewhere else. Why would you accept that?"

Kang is a strong advocate of independent women's clubs and said that was one of the reasons she was attracted to London City Lionesses.

"My first entree into women's football was Washington Spirit, in the United States, where two thirds of women's teams are independent and not affiliated with men's team. So to me, that's a lot more normal.

"I wanted to show that there isn't just one model that the women's team has to be part of the men's team, but an independent team, because I think at that time, London City and Durham, if I'm not mistaken, those are the two, women-only teams.

"I wanted to build a women-only team to show when you really devote all your attention and resources and energy into women's only team, what's possible."

Kang traces much of that belief back to her upbringing in South Korea and the influence of her father.

When asked why she is so passionate about women, Kang said: "I think it probably originally came from my father. From very early on, my father, who had only three girls. It maybe was a necessity.

"I was growing up in South Korea, where it was still a very traditional society, where girls have certain roles.

"He said in this day and age it doesn't matter whether you're a girl or a boy, whatever you want to do, you have to put 100% of what you have and you can go for it. And if you don't achieve, you have only yourself to blame."

Kang says those lessons have stayed with her throughout her career.

"I'm grateful that I achieved my American dream. And this is my way of giving back that I don't want, quite frankly, a lot of young girls growing up going through what I went through.

"I want them to be able to focus on what they have to do to be the best football player, not having to worry about changing clothes in the middle of a public park or broken equipment - all those type of things."

The club's training centre is also expected to support research into female athlete health, an area Kang believes has been overlooked for decades. Kang pointed to injury rates as one example.

"There are more ACL, injuries among female players. The tune of two or three times more female players get ACL injuries than male players," she said.

"Something like 94% of all science medical research is dedicated to men. So there's just fundamentally so little known about female body."

Kang's ambitions extend beyond London. Through her multi-club ownership model, which already spans England, France and the United States, she wants the standards being established at London City to be replicated across the globe.

"I would like to buy a team in Asia. I would like to buy a team in Africa. I would like to buy a team in South America, because I want all the girls in those countries to grow up thinking that this kind of the best, best, facilities and best practices and unbelievably, infrastructure is not something that they can only watch on TV because they're only in England, France, America, but it's in their backyard."

The owner says she wants future generations of female players to enjoy opportunities equal to those available to boys, regardless of where they grow up.

"That reality, the gap between the girls and boys journeys is indefensible, and I want that to disappear."

And when asked what message she had for the rest of the Women's Super League, her answer was short and direct.

title: Trump says he's banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House
description:
— President Donald Trump said Friday that he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage, and threatened that more such media prohibitions could be coming — offering his administration's latest test of constitutional First Amendment protections guaranteeing the freedom of the press.
Trump has long bristled at news coverage he maintains casts him in a negative light, and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organizations, while lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.
The move follows the president's decision, in February 2025, to keep Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet's decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico's name.
The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, however, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Friday that he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage, and threatened that more such media prohibitions could be coming — offering his administration's latest test of constitutional First Amendment protections guaranteeing the freedom of the press.

Trump has long bristled at news coverage he maintains casts him in a negative light, and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organizations, while lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.

The move follows the president's decision, in February 2025, to keep Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet's decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico's name.

The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, however, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC.

Trump seeking to block White House access for CNN is especially notably, however, as it could upend the traditional five-network television pool that travels with the president and tracks his every move — meant to provide independent coverage of his actions and interactions for the Americans who elected him and the world.

In the social media announcement, Trump did not provide details on how the ban would be implemented.

It came moments before Trump spoke to reporters in the Oval Office as part of a health care event. He later planned to take the press pool to his golf club in Virginia for a meeting and dinner sponsored by his Super PAC before spending the weekend at Camp David — one of the few places reporters don't follow him.

The president wrote on his social media site that effective immediately, "I am banning" CNN, MSNOW and Politico "from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!"

"Media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America," Trump wrote. "Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow."

title: Josh Allen on pace to surpass LaDainian Tomlinson’s single-season record
description: Allen is chasing an NFL record after a scorching start.
fullText:
The NFL has already seen Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen put himself on a remarkable pace after another dominant performance on the ground in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.

Allen rushed for two touchdowns against Detroit, matching his two rushing scores from Week 1. Through the first two games of the season, the 2024 NFL MVP has already found the end zone four times on the ground.

That puts Allen on pace for 34 rushing touchdowns over a 17-game season, which would surpass Hall of Fame running back LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season record of 28 rushing touchdowns, set in 2006.

Of course, maintaining that pace throughout an entire season would be an enormous challenge, but Allen's early production has put the record firmly in the conversation.

MORE: Lions coaching decision mistake proving to be epic failure

Sep 13, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) jogs on the field during the game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Allen's impact against the Lions wasn't limited to his rushing ability. The Bills quarterback also threw three touchdown passes, giving him five passing touchdowns through the opening two games of the season.

Thursday's performance also added another remarkable statistic to Allen's growing résumé. He recorded his 10th career game with at least two rushing touchdowns and two passing touchdowns.

No other quarterback has matched that total. Hall of Famer Steve Young is next on the all-time list, having accomplished the feat four times.

Allen's unique combination of passing and rushing production has become one of the defining features of his game. Last season, he finished with 14 rushing touchdowns and 25 passing touchdowns, showing just how frequently Buffalo relies on him near the goal line.

MORE: NFL bettor places wild wager on Miami Dolphins

Jan 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up before a game against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images

The Bills have opened the season 2-0, and Allen's production has played a major role in their fast start.

While four rushing touchdowns through two games does not guarantee that Allen will threaten Tomlinson's record by the end of the season, his current pace has certainly created an intriguing storyline to follow.

Buffalo will look to remain undefeated when it returns home in Week 3 to host the Los Angeles Chargers. If Allen continues finding the end zone at his current rate, the record chase could become one of the NFL's biggest stories as the season progresses.

title: 10 Keyboard Hacks Every iPhone User Should Know
description: These hacks help you make the most of typing on your iPhone.
fullText:
On the surface, the iPhone keyboard looks like it did a decade ago, but underneath, much has changed. In addition to the hidden features that have existed for years, Apple has slowly added features and gestures that make typing a bit easier. If you're still shaking your iPhone to undo text, it's time to dig deeper. These 10 hacks can help you make the most of typing on your iPhone.

Typing on an iPhone’s glass surface can feel a bit lifeless, especially if you’re used to typing on mechanical keyboards on your Mac. While there’s no way to get a physical keyboard on the iPhone (unless you get something like the Clicks keyboard), you can simulate it. The iPhone has a built-in Taptic engine, which provides subtle vibrations as you interact with the device. While most know it from notifications, calls, and scrolling through various iOS UI elements, it can be enabled for the keyboard too. Go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Keyboard Feedback and enable \"Haptic Feedback."

When you type on the iPhone keyboard, all you see are letters. To type numbers or symbols, you have to switch to the “123” keyboard layout instead—unless you use this hidden gesture, that is. See, each letter is already hiding a number or alternative symbol behind it. All you need to do to reveal it is to swipe from the 123 key. Once you do that, the keyboard will reveal numbers and symbols. Drag your finger to the number you want to enter, let go, and it’s done. The keyboard goes back to being a keyboard.

The iPhone has OCR (optical character recognition) built into iOS. You use this anytime you copy text from an image in the Photos app. The same feature is integrated into the Camera app, and lets you paste that text straight into any field, bypassing the keyboard entirely. To do so, point the camera towards any text, and the app will frame it in a yellow border. You’ll also see a Live Text button in the bottom-right corner. Tap on it, select the text, and tap the Copy button. Now, open any text field, and you’ll see a suggestion to paste the text you just copied.

If you have a large iPhone, typing with one hand can be extremely difficult. Instead, use the keyboard's one-handed mode. Tap and hold the Globe key to find options to dock the one-handed keyboard to the left or the right (below the list of all available keyboards). If you don’t see it, go to Settings > General > Keyboard > One-Handed Keyboard and choose Left or Right from here. Once enabled, you’ll see a shrunken keyboard layout docked to one side of the screen. Tap the Arrow button to change the docking position. Unfortunately, unlike Gboard on Android, you can’t resize the keyboard itself, but this does make it much easier to use your keyboard with one hand.

Apple’s built-in Text Replacement feature can transform a couple of pre-programmed letters into canned responses. That could be your address, an email template for clients, a signature, a repeated sign-off message, anything you frequently type. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard > Text Replacement. Here, tap the Plus button from the top, add the expanded response in the "Phrase" field and the trigger characters in the "Shortcut" field.

You can simply drag the iPhone’s cursor to select text. But instead of fiddling with the little cursor point, try tapping on the screen. You can double-tap a word to quickly select it; triple-tap, and you’ll select the sentence. Tap four times, and now the entire paragraph is selected.

Once you’ve selected the text, pinch in with three fingers to quickly copy the text. Pinch outwards with three fingers to paste the text. You can also swipe left with three fingers to undo anything you just did. For precise text selection, nothing beats the trackpad hack. You might already know that if you press and hold the Space bar on the iPhone keyboard, the whole thing turns into a trackpad. But you can also use this feature to select text. Keep your finger on the Space bar, but use another finger to move the cursor to select the text.

There may be times when the iPhone keyboard goes haywire. Autocorrect might keep suggesting words you never type, or it keeps bringing up specific casual words you type in a group chat, but don’t mean to repeat. If you’re fed up with keyboard suggestions, there is an out. You can reset the whole thing, starting fresh by rebuilding the suggestions library. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Keyboard Dictionary to get started.

If you’re multilingual, you might constantly switch between keyboards to type in your target language. Now, you don't need to do that. You can enable multilingual support to type in different languages on a single keyboard. When you enable two languages, the iPhone keyboard adapts automatically. It knows which language you’re typing and will even provide different suggestions based on it. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard. Choose a language, and then select if you want to add a new keyboard, or if you want to add the language to your existing keyboard.

You shouldn’t trust AI to write for you, but you can use it to proofread and edit text you’ve crafted yourself. And there’s no need to pay for an AI subscription either. If you have Apple Intelligence built into your iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro and later), you can use the Writing Tools feature instead. Writing Tools is integrated into the Notes app, Mail app, and basically anywhere you write text. Select the text, and from the pop-up menu, choose "Writing Tools." From here, ask Siri to make the text shorter, format it to make it sound more formal, and, of course, to check for grammar and spelling mistakes.

title: This New iOS 27 Feature May Save You From Getting Scammed
description: It's designed to detect and prevent social engineering scams.
fullText:
Starting with iOS 27, your iPhone now has a built-in scam prevention feature, designed to protect you from social engineering scams. These scams rely on pressure tactics to trick you into bypassing security features for your phone, laptop, or online accounts. Here's how iOS 27's "Impersonation Risk Detection" works, what it can do, and its current limitations.

In a social engineering scam, a bad actor impersonates an official rep of a bank, government agency, or a tech company such as Apple, Google, or Microsoft. The scammer may even impersonate your friends, family members, or colleagues you trust. They'll try to force you to disable account security measures such as two-factor authentication, or talk you into sharing your financial information. They'll create a fake problem, establish trust, and then pressure you into making large payments.

Apple says Impersonation Risk Detection can analyze information about your iPhone or iPad, your Apple Account, and check for signs of an active scam. Once it completes the analysis, iOS 27 will share a risk level with the app that's being targeted by scammers. Apple emphasizes that the app doesn't receive any data associated with your device or Apple Account that was used to assess the risk level.

From there, it's up to the app to decide how to proceed. If an app supports Impersonation Risk Detection, it may add a delay to each step you're trying to execute, show warnings, or even ask you to verify your identity. Apps can use various factors to decide if they need a risk assessment from iOS 27, which include big changes to your account, resetting its password, disabling two-factor authentication, making large payments, etc.

Once an app requests iOS 27 for a risk assessment, the operating system can conduct an analysis and place the action into one of three risk level markers (again, Apple doesn't control what apps do with the risk level information):

Unknown: This means that iOS 27 couldn't detect any suspicious activity. Apple says that doesn't mean the action was confirmed as safe.

Medium: This risk level is assigned when iOS 27 detects some signs of suspicious activity.

High: This risk level is associated with significant signs of suspicious activity.

Once you've updated your iPhone to iOS 27 (or your iPad to iPadOS 27), go to Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom, and tap Impersonation Risk Detection. Enable the toggle next to "Share with App Developers." Now, tap Share with App Developers in the pop-up. Once Impersonation Risk Detection is enabled, you don't need to take further action. Note that when you try to disable this feature, it may take up to 24 hours to take effect. This is to protect you from scammers, who may pressure you into disabling the feature.

In the same settings page, you'll be able to see which app requested access to your risk levels, and why. This will show up under the "Recent Activity" section. You'll also be able to turn off this feature for individual apps that appear in this section, but, again, it may take up to 24 hours to disable the setting.

Security features are only as strong as their weakest links. In the case of iOS 27's Impersonation Risk Detection, there are two main weak links. First, this feature is disabled by default. Most people aren't going to dig deep enough into settings to discover it accidentally, and the feature isn't going to be used widely unless people know about it. Second, this feature also depends on app developers adding support for it. Big tech companies and indie developers may adopt it reasonably quickly, but other developers may not rush to implement this feature.

There's also the fact that plenty of apps have already spent a lot of resources building up their own security infrastructure, and they may not necessarily see value in adding support for this feature. Here in India, all banking and payment apps show multiple full-screen warnings when you try to make a payment while on a phone call. Some apps may even disable payment features if they detect that a screen-sharing app is installed on your device. So, really, it will come down to how app developers respond to this feature.

Apple says that Impersonation Risk Detection performs its analysis on-device, and that the data used to generate the risk level doesn't leave your device. The company also highlights that the contents of your email, photos, or messages are not analyzed for the risk assessment. When an app requests a risk assessment, Apple claims it only receives information about the type of action you performed in that specific app. Once the risk level is generated, apps don't receive any additional data about you.

title: OpenAI ‘ethically hacked’ with help of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot
description:
US cybersecurity researchers who conducted hack say ‘scope of what we could theoretically access was huge’
Cybersecurity researchers have hacked into OpenAI with the help of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot, in the latest example of security issues at the company.
A team at a US-based startup compromised a number of OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts, starting a process that enabled them to access their target’s software cache – and potentially more.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
US cybersecurity researchers who conducted hack say ‘scope of what we could theoretically access was huge’

Cybersecurity researchers have hacked into OpenAI with the help of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot, in the latest example of security issues at the company.

A team at a US-based startup compromised a number of OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts, starting a process that enabled them to access their target’s software cache – and potentially more.

“The scope of what we could theoretically access was huge,” said researchers at Hacktron AI.

Initially, the research team used Claude, which can generate code for hackers, to access ChatGPT accounts via an OpenAI staff discussion forum hosted by the Discourse platform. They then made a harmless “pull request” – an attempt to change the code in a file – to OpenAI’s service on the GitHub software repository.

Hacktron reported the hack to OpenAI, having carried out the operation under an OpenAI programme that rewarded ethical hackers for testing its systems. The researchers stressed that they had access to, but did not download, the code from the GitHub repository.

Despite initial use of Claude, the researchers said they were largely using OpenAI’s own cutting edge GPT-5.6 Sol model to carry out the hack, which was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

An OpenAI spokesperson said: “We thank the researchers for contacting us and sharing their findings”, adding that the company had addressed the vulnerabilities that had been exploited.

Hacktron said AI tools had made a once-complex hacking task far easier and drastically shortened the time needed to plan and execute an attack. This is a common refrain from cybersecurity experts when discussing the impact of AI.

“Work that once required a well-resourced team and months of effort can now be compressed into days,” said Hacktron, which received a $6,500 payment from OpenAI under the company’s bug bounty programme.

The hack is the latest safety incident at OpenAI, which revealed in July that a “swarm” of agents – the term for AI tools capable of carrying out tasks autonomously – powered by its technology had hacked the AI startup Hugging Face during a cybersecurity test.

This week the San Francisco-based company revealed six more examples of “unexpected or concerning” actions by its technology, and warned that the pace of development could not continue at “maximum speed for much longer”.

Anthropic made a fresh call at the weekend for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Elon Musk. Anthropic also repeated warnings that unrestrained AI development posed an existential threat, concerns that some experts are sceptical about.

Donald Trump has rejected calls for a slowdown, citing a need to stay ahead of China’s AI industry and dismissing “negative forces … bringing up things that won’t happen”.

title: Derby day deluge - five things to watch in the EFL
description: Local rivalries, competitive cities, or simply a team named Derby coming to town - here are five things to look out for across the weekend in the EFL.
fullText:
Derby delights abound in the English Football League this weekend.

Whether it be local rivalries, competitive cities, or simply a team named Derby coming to town, for many the biggest thing on offer will not just be about the league table.

Here are five things to look out across the weekend in the EFL.

A match between a relegated club and a team who missed out on a play-off spot on the final day of the season sounds like a treat - but for fans of Burnley and Derby County, it is a recipe for a potential nightmare.

Neither team has made a good start, to put it mildly.

The Clarets are bottom and still looking for their first win; Derby have amassed just four points in seven games and are on a three-match losing streak.

It is too early to say both are relegation candidates but the signs are worrying and Saturday's meeting at Turf Moor (15:00 BST) feels like it will carry more weight than it should.

What is worse for the Rams is Sweden international goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom has been ruled out of the match with a knee problem.

"The defensive aspect for Derby at the moment is under scrutiny, we are conceding goals, and to lose your first-choice goalkeeper is a big blow," former Rams academy coach Darren Robinson told BBC Radio Derby.

Rams keeper Zetterstrom out with knee injury

Walker 'desperate' to end Burnley's winless woe

The bitterness of losing a derby can linger far beyond the season.

West Ham went a man down in the ninth minute the last time they met Millwall in 2012, but they still managed to claw out a 2-1 victory.

It would have left a scar on the Lions, who have seen their storming start to the Championship falter in the past few games, while their London rivals have leapt to the top following an unsteady start on their return to the Championship.

They meet at The Den on Saturday (12:30 BST) with the Hammers chasing a fifth straight victory and aiming to fully establish their position as league leaders.

Meanwhile, Molineux hosts its first Black Country derby since 2021 on Sunday (12:00 BST).

Wolves lost 3-2 in this fixture when West Bromwich Albion visited most recently but, like Millwall, it is 2012 that truly haunts them.

Baggies boss James Morrison played his hand in a 5-1 victory for Albion on the pitch that day and 14 years later he will be hoping to inflict further suffering from the dugout.

Rivalries renewed: The derby games back this season

Quiz: Can you remember West Ham & Millwall's last derby?

Quiz: How well do you know the Black Country derby?

Wolves striker Jimenez to miss derby with West Brom

Wolves and Albion issue warning over derby disorder

Cambridge and Oxford are cities with a rivalry for the ages.

Both striving for the highest echelons of academics, their famed universities usually find themselves in a boat race for their bragging rights. But in football, they have another ambition in mind.

After impressive starts, it appears both Cambridge United and Oxford United are on the hunt for promotion.

Cambridge have adjusted excellently to life in League One under Neil Harris to suffer just one defeat in six games (W3 D2), while Aaron Ramsey's Oxford are overcoming a transfer embargo and relegation disappointment to do the same in five (W3 D1).

Both are in a play-off position, just one point separating the two, and with such interlinked history within the cities their game on Saturday (15:00 BST) feels like it is going to be good.

Doncaster manager Grant McCann recently revealed he was diagnosed with skin cancer last year and while he says he has recovered now, it can put events on the football pitch into perspective.

His team are technically under pressure - bottom of the league and without a win to their name (D3 L3).

Doncaster next visit Peterborough United on Saturday (15:00 BST), a club McCann has rich history with as both a player and a manager.

Peterborough are only two points ahead and in danger themselves.

A familiar ground against an opponent of similar form can sometimes bring stress, but it can also mean opportunity.

"I'm not putting any extra on the pressure to the players, if anything I'm feeling a bit calmer," McCann told BBC Radio Sheffield.

"Nobody wants to be in position where we haven't won in six games but if we look at all the games, we've had really good opportunities to put the game away.

"We haven't quite done that but we have to stay on top of what we believe in and it will certainly come."

Doncaster boss McCann reveals skin cancer treatment

You think the Championship is the only place you can catch derby drama this weekend? Think again.

Saturday's early kick-offs in League Two offer a double helping of local rivals going at it.

The Premier League's Manchester derby between City and United was the cause of much conversation this week but while Oldham and Rochdale (12:30 BST) are likely to fly much lower under the radar, it is worth its own talking point.

Both have recently returned to the EFL from the National League but Rochdale have not yet found their footing and will be seeking just their second win of the season to start settling in.

However, Oldham have lost their past two in succession and are at risk at tumbling down the down the table after a solid start to their campaign.

Meanwhile, Port Vale make the short trip from Burslem to Walsall (12:30 BST).

The Saddlers watched Vale win promotion ahead of them during a rollercoaster 2024-25 season, but the Valiants are back in the fourth tier and struggling.

Vale are just above the relegation line after claiming their first win of the season against Exeter City last weekend and will aim to back it up against a Walsall team who have proven a tricky team for them in the past.

This exact fixture was claimed by the Valiants last time out but the Saddlers were unbeaten in their previous seven meetings, winning six.

To make the Saddlers even more of threat, they have gone undefeated in the league so far and will want to stay that way.

First win can give us confidence - Vale boss Brady

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action, starting with Bristol City v Watford (20:00 BST) on Friday, throughout Saturday's fixtures and culminating in Norwich City v Bolton Wanderers on Sunday (13:30 BST).

title: Adams Verling handed Ireland debut for WXV opener
description: Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling is handed her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin.
fullText:
Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling will make her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin.

Adams Verling will line out at blind-side flanker in the back row alongside captain Erin King at open-side flanker and Women's Six Nations player of the championship Aoife Wafer at number eight.

The 20-year-old's ascension to the senior team comes after she impressed in the U18 Women's Six Nations in 2024 and last year's U21 Women's Six Nations while she has also been impressive for the Clovers in the Celtic Challenge.

She was part of this year's Six Nations squad but did not feature.

Head coach Scott Bemand has named an experienced pack with props Niamh O'Dowd and Linda Djougang and hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald in the front row.

With Sam Monaghan out injured, Dorothy Wall and Fiona Tuite-O'Sullivan line up in the second row.

In the back three, Stacey Flood starts at full-back with Robyn O'Connor and Vicky Elmes Kinlan on the wings. Right winger O'Connor was one of Ireland's breakout players in this year's Six Nations, scoring two tries.

Aoife Dalton and Eve Higgins start in midfield, while Dannah O'Brien and Emily Lane retain their half-back partnership from the Six Nations.

The forward replacements are Neve Jones, Sadhbh McGrath, Eilis Cahill, Jane Clohessy and Brittany Hogan, who scored five tries in this year's Six Nations, with Aoibheann Reilly, Anna McGann and Niamh Gallagher offering backline cover.

Ireland open their WXV Global Series campaign against the United States at Dublin's Tallaght Stadium (13:45 BST), the first women's rugby Test match at the home of football team Shamrock Rovers.

Bemand's side then face Japan in a double-header in Galway and Cork on 27 September and 3 October - the first of which is a WXV game - before WXV games against South Africa in Cape Town on 24 and 31 October.

Ireland: Flood; O'Connor, Dalton, Higgins, Elmes Kinlan; O'Brien, Lane; O'Dowd, Moloney-MacDonald, Djougang, Wall, Tuite-O'Sullivan, Adams Verling, King (capt), Wafer

Replacements: Jones, McGrath, Cahill, Clohessy, Hogan, Reilly, McGann, Gallagher

title: Saints drop plan for memorial wall for fans' ashes
description: The club says there has not been enough demand for the project.
fullText:
A plan for a memorial wall that would have included the ashes of Northampton Saints rugby fans has been cancelled.

The Saints Memorial Wall was to have been part of a wider development to enhance the fan village at the Prem Rugby side's Franklin's Gardens ground.

However, the club said initial demand "was not sufficient to support the long-term viability of the development".

Supporters who have already paid will receive a refund, Saints said.

"When we launched the Saints Memorial Wall, we did so believing it could provide a meaningful and lasting tribute for supporters and their loved ones at the heart of Franklin's Gardens," said the club's chief executive, Julia Chapman.

"Having carefully reviewed the level of demand we concluded that it was not right for us to proceed with the project.

"This was not a decision we took lightly and we recognise that it will be disappointing for some supporters.

"While that is a source of genuine regret, we hope they will understand the reasons behind our decision," she added.

When the project was announced the club said ashes would be interred for 50 years, with costs ranging from £4,000 to £8,000.

Alternative ways for supporters to "create a lasting legacy" at the ground will be explored, it added.

title: Sorensen to join Republic of Ireland coaching staff
description: Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen is set to join the Republic of Ireland squad for their Women's World Cup play-off qualifiers this year.
fullText:
Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen is set to join the Republic of Ireland squad for their Women's World Cup play-off qualifiers this year.

Sorensen is expected to take up the role of assistant coach in their set-up, alongside Liverpool's Amber Whiteley.

It is understood he will retain his position as technical director with Aston Villa women, but will link up with the Republic of Ireland during the international break.

He will work with manager Carla Ward, who faced Sorensen's Everton in the Women's Super League when she managed Villa.

The Republic of Ireland play Kazakhstan in the first round of play-off qualifying; the two-legged tie will take place on 9 and 13 October.
