title: Somerset title hopes fade after defeat by Yorkshire
description: Somerset's hopes of a first-ever County Championship title are dented with a heavy defeat at Yorkshire.
fullText:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Headingley (day four)

Yorkshire 212 & 275: Hill 89, Bess 77; Overton 3-44

Somerset 201: Cliff 8-76 & 101: Lammonby 32; Coad 4-33

Yorkshire (19 pts) beat Somerset (3 pts) by 185 runs

A relentless Yorkshire bowling performance put a significant dent in Somerset's County Championship title challenge, the hosts consigning the pre-game Division One leaders to a hammer-blow defeat at Headingley.

Somerset, who were chasing 287, started day four on 73-3, quickly slipped to 79-6 and were later bowled out for 101 just before 12:00 BST to lose by 185 runs.

A third defeat of the season, and a second against Yorkshire, means that Warwickshire now lead Division One by 11 points from second-placed Somerset, who have never won this title. Nottinghamshire will also be in the mix come next week's final round, even if they lose against Sussex later on Friday.

For the mid-table White Rose, they claimed their fifth win in 13 games and backed up May's success at Taunton. New ball seamers Ben Coad and Ben Cliff starred on Friday, Coad finishing with four wickets and Cliff three.

Outstanding Cliff ended with career-best match figures of 11-105, the 13th best match analysis in his county's first-class history.

Cliff and Coad struck in the space of five balls inside the day's opening half hour, putting Yorkshire on course for a 19-point haul to Somerset's three.

They removed not out batters Tom Lammonby and Tom Abell as Somerset lost two wickets for the addition of only three runs - 76-5.

Lammonby was squared up and caught behind off Cliff for 32 before Abell looped a catch up to backward point off the shoulder of the bat against Coad.

And when Coad struck again almost three overs later, at the end of the 39th, Somerset were in significant trouble, with James Rew caught at second slip on the drive.

Yorkshire came into day four knowing they had the edge but one wicket they were desperate for was that of Craig Overton, who had broken their hearts back in July here with a stunning 79 not out off 30 balls in the Vitality Blast quarter-final.

Cliff got him caught behind pushing forwards in the 42nd over for five, also trapping Lewis Gregory lbw three balls later.

At 88-8, it was all but game over under an overcast Headingley sky but not quite matching the gloomy Somerset outlook.

The Overton and Gregory wickets were Cliff's 10th and 11th in the match following his eight in the first innings.

Like Overton, Migael Pretorius had scored a first-innings fifty. But George Hill had him caught behind, leaving Somerset at 92-9.

Matthew Revis then wrapped things up by yorking Jake Ball, with day four lasting only 82 minutes in all.

Somerset face Surrey at the Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton, in the final round of fixtures, which starts on Thursday, while Yorkshire can continue to play the role of spoilers when they travel to face Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.

title: 'You have to start somewhere' - inexperienced GB team bid for Davis Cup Finals
description: Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.
fullText:
Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.

British number two Norrie felt pain in his arm during a practice session and will be replaced in Saturday's singles by world number 95 Toby Samuel.

"He wasn't able to accelerate on the ball like he wanted to," Davis Cup captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.

"It's nothing major, but there's still a lot of tennis to be played this year and with that in mind, we had to make the difficult decision to replace him."

Great Britain have not reached the knockout stage of the competition since 2023, and they will have to do so this time with an inexperienced team.

Jack Draper has ended his difficult season early, while Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley are both unavailable with injury.

It means Samuel will make his Davis Cup debut against Andres Andrade in Saturday's first match, with British number one Arthur Fery following against Alvaro Guillen Meza.

Both of Ecuador's singles players are outside the world's top 200, but Fery's only previous appearance for his country was in Poland last September.

Asked if he was concerned about the lack of experience, Smith said: "I'm not sure it concerns me, but it is obviously a factor.

"Neal [Skupski] is in the team, Cam is staying with the team. I've had 16 years at this so I can hopefully help a little bit.

"But you want them to experience this. You have to start somewhere and I have a lot of confidence in Arthur, Toby and our doubles team.

"If they can put out the level of tennis we've seen over the course of the summer and before that, they'll give themselves a good opportunity."

British number seven Harry Wendelken, who is at a career-high world ranking of 175, was at the Copper Box as a practice partner and has been added to the team in Norrie's absence.

World number one Henry Patten will team up with new US Open champion Neal Skupski for Sunday's doubles, which precedes two reverse singles.

Davis Cup: Great Britain v Ecuador

Coverage from 13:00 BST on 19 September and 12:00 BST on 20 September

In July, Fery played on Wimbledon's Centre Court in a men's singles semi-final, but this will be the first time he has played for his country as the British number one.

He lost in the first round of the US Open in August but reached the Winston-Salem final in the build-up to the final Grand Slam of the season.

"I'm aware of the role I have as the number one player and I am representing my country, so there's always a little more responsibility," Fery told BBC Sport.

"But at the same time I've been able to deal with high-pressure situations a lot of times this year and I feel like I've done a great job with them. Tomorrow isn't going to be any different to that.

"I think there's no shying away from it - if I want to do great things in tennis and push on, be top 20 or top 10, I have to take this responsibility on.

"I'm ready to do that and represent my country. It's something new but something that I feel comes with the player I'm becoming."

Great Britain beat Norway 4-0 in the first qualifying round in February and are trying to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 2023.

Ecuador may be the underdogs, but they were in the same role when they beat Australia comprehensively in February.

And they have won, famously, on British soil before. Ecuador beat a British team that contained Tim Henman and Greg Rusedski 3-2 on Wimbledon's Court One in July 2000.

The seven winners of this weekend's qualifying ties will join three-time defending champions Italy in the final eight stage in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

"We've missed not being at that stage and it's up to us now to take that opportunity," Smith added.

"We have a good opportunity. It's never ever straightforward, despite what people might look at in the rankings - just ask Australia what happened in February.

"We're on it, we've got a good team, and we'd be thrilled to get to the finals."

title: Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning
description: England boss Thomas Tuchel recalls Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer but says players have to "perform".
fullText:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel says "the door is always open" after recalling Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer to his first squad since the World Cup - but has warned players they have to "perform".

Tuchel controversially left Real Madrid right-back Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Palmer out of his squad for the summer tournament in North America.

Both return for four Nations League games during an extended international break after this weekend's club fixtures.

Alexander-Arnold, 27, won the most recent of his 34 England caps when he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 win against Andorra in June 2025.

He has made five appearances, including three starts, for Real Madrid so far this season, registering one assist.

Palmer, 24, last played for England in a 1-0 friendly defeat by Japan in March. He has scored four goals and provided two assists in six games this season.

"They had a good start to the season," said Tuchel, who has again omitted Manchester City's Phil Foden. "They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad.

"I think he has a point to prove, and the same goes for Trent. He was never off the list. He was never non-selectable for us, and it is his chance to show, come to camp and be the best version of himself."

Alexander-Arnold played in midfield in Real's Champions League win over Inter Milan earlier this month, but Tuchel said he had picked the former Liverpool player as a full-back.

"He had a good start in two positions for Real Madrid and he comes as a right-back for us," he said.

On his trust in Alexander Arnold, Tuchel said: "[He needs to] perform, that's just what it is. It is a competition and I understand the question because he was not with us at the World Cup. We trusted other players.

"I still stick with this decision and it is now time to fight for his place. He always said he is up for a fight, he always said he is up to fight for his place - especially for England - so it is on him to prove and he is more than welcome in camp.

"We have a long camp and I am sure he will show up."

Tuchel said the onus was now on players to impress in the international set-up.

"It is one thing to be nominated, like with Cole, and getting your ticket back in the squad but it's another thing to perform for England," he said.

"Cole needs to step up when he comes and he needs to show these kind of numbers to get his place, keep his shirt and justify the nomination."

Giving a message to his players, he later told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Jordan Henderson said it so professionally well before the match against France - you just never know when your next England match is coming.

"So, guys, this is it - this is the next England match you play to the fullest, you show up with the right attitude, and you give it your all, because you never know.

"It is not even a shout-out to Trent; it is a shout-out to everyone. It's the mentality that we want to have.

"If you come to camp it is not an international break, it's an international window."

England host World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September, then travel to Czech Republic (Tuesday, 29 September) and Croatia (Saturday, 3 October) before the Czechs visit on Tuesday, 6 October.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha, who were both in the Three Lions' pre-World Cup squad, both feature again.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin, whose three top-flight goals so far this season have helped Leeds United go third in the Premier League, is also included.

Tuchel has also picked Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall, Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite, Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play at left-back or in midfield, and Brighton keeper Jason Steele.

Dean Henderson, Jordan Henderson, Reece James, Djed Spence and John Stones, who were all in the World Cup squad, miss out, with Tuchel saying they were not selected because of injuries.

Along with Foden, other notable absentees are Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White, Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton and Manchester United's Harry Maguire.

Tuchel regrets not eating Azteca turf after win over Mexico

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton), James Trafford (Leeds United)

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trevoh Chalobah (Como), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Tino Livramento (Newcastle United), Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen)

Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Alex Scott (Bournemouth)

Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Marcus Rashford (Manchester United), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea), Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)

The Nations League matches will be England's first since the 2026 World Cup, where they were beaten in the semi-finals by Argentina.

The Three Lions took a 1-0 lead but conceded two late goals, with former England captain Wayne Rooney saying the team "crumbled" and became "too passive", which he said started from "the manager and the decisions he made".

Though England missed out on their first men's World Cup final in 60 years, they beat France 6-4, having led 4-0 at half-time, in an thrilling bronze-medal match.

"The more I reflect on it, it's maybe more buying into our strengths and playing more minutes like we played in the second half against Croatia and the first half against France," said Tuchel.

"Buying into these strengths because we get a lot of value out of it. We get a lot of connection to the fans. This is what the Premier League reflects.

"Football is about adapting to situations, and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach if you look at the 6-4 against France - but people talk about it like it's one of their most nicest experiences ever.

"Maybe I have to compromise in my wish and urge for control - for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best [in us].

"We will adjust our style but always to put the strengths of the players as the first priority."

Tuchel's defensive substitutions were called into question following the defeat by Argentina, but he played down how much of an issue that was with England supporters.

"I tell you something, 99.9% of the fans don't speak about substitutions and tactical things," he said.

"They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second-half energy of the Croatia match. They speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against DR Congo and where they celebrated.

"This is the feedback that I get. This is what we created and how it should be.

"This is what a World Cup is for, to connect with people and give them experiences that they do not forget. It makes me proud."

The Football Association has conducted what Tuchel described as a "sometimes painful, sometimes emotional" review into England's World Cup campaign.

Tuchel said he felt "support from all my bosses" at the tournament and "there was never a doubt in my mind or their mind that we will continue together".

Among the highlights of the Three Lions' tournament was a 3-2 defeat of co-hosts Mexico at the Azteca Stadium, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men following Jarell Quansah's red card.

"It was a very special moment before the Mexico game, where we had a talk and my bosses told me we know anything can happen in a football game, and in Mexico," said Tuchel.

"'Don't worry, we see what is going on and we want to continue like this.' It is a beautiful moment for me as a coach."

Since the World Cup, Fifa president Gianni Infantino has come under increasing pressure following a failed plan to sell off stakes in competitions to private investors, and for the manner in which United States forward Folarin Balogun had a suspension overturned.

Balogun was sent off during his side's win against Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last 32 but was allowed to play against Belgium in the last 16 when he would have expected to be serving a one-match suspension.

That came after US President Donald Trump asked Fifa to review it.

The FA has withdrawn its support for Infantino's re-election and asked him to release all documents relating to both controversies.

"I told you how I am backed from my bosses so the minimum I can do is back my bosses," said Tuchel.

"They have my full support on that and back their opinion. I'm grateful that I can talk about football, that's my little bit of knowledge that I have and not about sport politics."

title: Hampshire relegated as Leicestershire keep survival hopes alive
description: Hampshire are relegated from Division One as Leicestershire chase a target of 334 to keep their own survival hopes alive.
fullText:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Uptonsteel Grace Road, Leicester (day four)

Hampshire 214 & 363: Gubbins 133; A Patel 4-103

Leicestershire 244 & 335-5: Kelly 86, Cox 75*

Leicestershire (19 pts) beat Hampshire (3 pts) by five wickets

Hampshire have been relegated to Division Two of the County Championship for the first time since winning promotion in 2014 after Leicestershire completed a five-wicket win at Uptonsteel Grace Road.

New Zealand international Nick Kelly and wicketkeeper Ben Cox did the heavy lifting for Leicestershire, backing up skipper Ian Holland's nine-wicket contribution to the win by sharing a 158-run fifth-wicket partnership as the home side chased down the 334 they needed to win.

It wrapped up victory by 14:05 BST with only two wickets lost on the final day.

The result means Leicestershire retain a mathematical chance of survival going into the final week of the season despite the 27-point penalty they were handed on Wednesday for preparing a sub-standard pitch for last month's win over Glamorgan, although it is a near certainty that they too will be playing in Division Two next year.

While the punishment remains subject to appeal, the only way Leicestershire can avoid going down is by wrecking Warwickshire's anticipated title celebrations with victory at Edgbaston next week and in doing so taking 20 more points than Essex pick up from their concluding fixture, away to Glamorgan.

The Foxes, who ended a 23-year-exile from Division One when they were promoted as Division Two champions last season, began the final day needing 178 more runs for victory, with Hampshire looking to take seven more wickets to keep their season alive.

With home supporters eager for the boost of a victory ahead of Sunday's One-Day Cup final against Middlesex, Kelly began with two eye-catching cover drives off Scott Currie for a couple of early boundaries.

Leicestershire suffered a setback as Hamza Shaikh, defending, was caught behind off a thin outside edge, giving Kyle Abbott his 62nd wicket of the campaign.

Yet it became clear the pitch - prepared in much the same away as the offending Glamorgan strip with grass in the middle and two shaved ends - had become somewhat less hazardous for the batting side than earlier in the contest.

Moreover, Hampshire struggled to contain them in any meaningful way. Off-spinner Felix Organ offered control at one end, Abbott was as disciplined as ever and James Fuller tidy, but Manny Lumsden, the 17-year-old who bowled so impressively against Nottinghamshire last week, rarely hit the right lengths this time and leaked runs as a consequence.

The fifth-wicket pair found enough singles too to keep the scoreboard moving without risking too much.

After Cox, who looks unlikely to be with the county next season, had driven Lumsden to the off-side rope to bring the requirement down to exactly 100, Kelly completed his third half-century in Leicestershire colours. Three boundaries then conceded by Lumsden in the final over of the morning left the home side just 67 runs from victory.

Soon afterwards Cox, who has been almost flawless behind the stumps all season, also passed 50 from 76 balls and even the return of Abbott and Currie with the new ball did not change the direction of travel, although there was a reminder the surface still had the capacity to surprise when the left-hander Kelly took a nasty blow on his right-hand.

A couple of painkillers later, though, he was back in full flow, hammering four boundaries in the same over off the unfortunate Lumsden.

Although he was ultimately caught on the rope aiming to finish things in style, the job was all but done, with Cox hitting what turned out to be the winning boundary off a Lumsden no-ball, his eighth of the match.

title: Wilson major Wales injury concern for Nations League
description: Leeds United forward Harry Wilson is a major doubt for the start of Wales' Nations League campaign because of a leg muscle injury.
fullText:
Harry Wilson is a major doubt for the start of Wales' Nations League campaign as they return to League A.

The Leeds United forward had been named in Craig Bellamy's squad to face Portugal, Denmark and Norway in September and October.

But Wilson's club boss Daniel Farke confirmed on Friday the 29-year-old has suffered a muscle injury to his quadriceps that will rule him out of Sunday's Premier League game at home to Crystal Palace.

"Harry Wilson is out of this game, a quad injury, he reported some problems after the last game and also during this training week," Farke said of the 69-cap player who has scored 17 times for his country.

"He will also probably miss the Welsh games, so definitely not good news for him and also not for the Welsh team."

While Wales may want to do their own assessment, the news is already a major blow for Bellamy given Wilson's outstanding international form over the past 12 months.

Bellamy is already without key defender Joe Rodon, Wilson's team-mate at Elland Road, as well as Cardiff City defensive pair Dylan Lawlor and Ronan Kpakio.

Two more Cardiff players, forwards Isaak Davies and Rubin Colwill are also unavailable for selection because of injury, along with Wrexham attacker Nathan Broadhead.

Wales travel to face Portugal on 24 September in the first of four fixtures in this newly extended international break, with a home match against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway sandwiched by two games with Denmark.

Wales - 38th in the world rankings, their lowest position since August 2014 - then travel to Copenhagen to take on a Denmark side ranked 21st in the world.

Norway, who were World Cup quarter-finalists, then visit Cardiff on 1 October before the return home game against Denmark on 4 October.

title: How Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Slot era
description: BBC Sport looks at how new manager Andoni Iraola is moving Liverpool on from the Arne Slot era after their disappointing form last season.
fullText:
Only 12 months ago Liverpool had won each of their first five Premier League games and were seemingly on their way to defending their crown under Arne Slot.

That run started with victory over a Bournemouth side led by Andoni Iraola on the opening night of the season.

Surely no one thought then that, come the end of the campaign, Iraola would be replacing Slot at Anfield.

Such is the volatility of football, it is too early to pass judgement on Iraola - even if his Liverpool side are already six points worse off than they were at this stage last season.

Under the 44-year-old, Liverpool are still unbeaten and this weekend Iraola returns to the place he called home for three years.

It will certainly be an odd feeling when he enters the smaller away changing room at Bournemouth - the Cherries have had to renovate it to comply with Europa League regulations, so at least it will be a slightly more pleasant experience than it would have been previously.

Iraola has swapped the seaside on the south coast for the beach town of Formby, where former Liverpool managers Jurgen Klopp and Brendan Rodgers also resided. By all accounts, he is settling in well. He has been spotted in the city centre on a few occasions and, as a keen cyclist, has enjoyed the coastal routes.

But Iraola is most at home on the training ground. He is very much a 'six days a week' coach, according to those at Liverpool, and such is his passion for coaching that he is often the first on the training pitch, marking the cones out for sessions.

"It's really intense. There's a lot of hard work and no sort of light days. Everyone's putting in 100%," said forward Lewis Koumas.

Those at Liverpool are firmly of the belief that everyone associated with the club was glad to get last season out of the way and that even if Slot had remained as head coach, things were always going to feel better.

At Liverpool's AXA Training Centre in Kirkby, Iraola rarely uses his own office and is often found in the coaches room where his assistants in Tommy Elphick, Shaun Cooper and Pablo de la Torre are based, and he has a relatively low-key presence in and around the building, compared to previous managers.

De la Torre, who moved with Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth in 2023, is seen as a key pillar in ensuring that the players are all up to the physical standard that Iraola wants.

In terms of actual changes inside the club they are not as big as people may think from the outside, given the structured nature of the head coach role.

Iraola's appointment was based on his fine work at Bournemouth but he is very much learning on the job when it comes to dealing with Liverpool's congested schedule.

There is a willingness to listen to other departments like the medical and fitness teams at Kirkby as the Reds seek to manage a squad that will play at least 49 games this season - a number that could climb into the 60s depending on Liverpool's cup runs.

When it comes to the training schedule, Iraola tends to adapt it in line with the kick-off time for the following fixture, with late afternoon and early evening sessions increasingly common. Under Slot, Liverpool tended to train at a similar time each day.

There have also been conversations with the academy and Rob Page, who coaches Liverpool Under-21s.

"We have an understanding of how the first team play and key principles, like how we press, how he [Iraola] wants his number 10 to press, how he wants his number eight to press, how he wants his centre-backs to press - we mirror that absolutely," said Page.

Earlier this week, Dominik Szoboszlai explained how Liverpool play with a number six, a number eight and a number 10 - and, despite calls for a defensive midfielder from fans during the transfer window, Iraola's system can work if everyone improves collectively.

Iraola's preference is to name the team on the morning of the game and he saves the post-match debrief with his players for the day after the match.

There is a sense of pragmatism with his media interactions, too, after a situation where his comments to LFC TV following a pre-season friendly against Monaco were widely reported.

Iraola conceded Liverpool had run out of steam after 30 minutes and did not have the energy levels at the time to play with the intensity that he wants. It wasn't meant to be a dig at his players - rather an admittance that they were working on building that intensity up.

But there is a realisation that at a club like Liverpool, every word you say can end up shared across social media and taken in a different way than you meant. That said, Iraola comes across as calm in his news conferences and open to discussion.

It is very much a case of Iraola adapting to the club as much as the other way round.

One of the main reasons they went for Iraola was his ability to develop young talent and the average age of Liverpool's players in the Premier League this season is 25.3 - only five teams have a lower average.

Youngsters like Rio Ngumoha, 18, Trey Nyoni, 19, and Koumas, 20, all started against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup and all three will play bigger roles this season than last.

Intensity is a buzzword under Iraola and that is a non-negotiable but he is already aware that, with such a brutal schedule, Liverpool will need to find ways to adapt and occasionally win games with a set-piece or an individual moment of brilliance.

Going into this weekend, they have made the most sprints in the Premier League but looked flat against Fulham last weekend in a goalless draw, less than 72 hours after beating Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Sunday's game against Bournemouth will be a fourth in 12 days and, after the international break, Liverpool have a spell of four games in 10 days. Between 11 October and 7 November, they will play nine times.

Iraola would no doubt have had a smile seeing Bournemouth win on their Europa League bow against Real Sociedad on Thursday, in the Basque region where he grew up.

Perhaps he will have a moment on the flight down from Liverpool on Saturday to think about how far he has come.

Liverpool haven't exactly had a dream start under Iraola but they are yet to lose. Becoming a team that is hard to beat is undoubtedly a step in the right direction after 12 league losses last term, but as vice-captain Alisson said last week, draws aren't good enough for Liverpool.

And Iraola, who is unbeaten in the Premier League since January across his two clubs, knows that a win on familiar territory on Sunday would be the perfect way to head into the international break.

title: Disgraceful nothing has changed after Tarling death - Brennan
description: Britain's Matthew Brennan says it is "disgraceful that nothing has changed" in cycling to make the sport safer following the death of Fin Tarling last month.
fullText:
Britain's Matthew Brennan says it is "disgraceful that nothing has changed" in cycling to make the sport safer following the death of Fin Tarling last month.

Britain's Tarling, 19, died on 14 August during the Volta a Portugal following a high-speed collision with a van which had strayed on to the closed road.

His funeral took place in Aberystwyth on Thursday.

Brennan, 21, who races for Dutch team Visma-Lease a Bike, told BBC Sport: "It was very sad what happened with Fin. We were watching his funeral yesterday and I said to my friend: 'It's so sad we've lost someone so special and also nothing has changed.'

"I really think that is disgraceful. Instead of someone somewhere in these organisations saying: 'OK, this should never ever happen again', it feels the world has moved on, nothing has changed and there's events where cars have been on the course still."

Six riders have died during road races in the past three years, and American rider Ezra Caudell is currently in hospital, external with "multi-system trauma" following a crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic.

Brennan, who won five stages at the recent three-week Vuelta a Espana Grand Tour, believes there should be an independent body to force through safety requirements at races.

"It's unbelievable, because you've lost a friend and when nothing changes it is really shocking.

"I think these big organisations and [sport's world governing body] the UCI should have a look at what they need to do to increase the safety.

"In my personal opinion, there should be an independent organisation that holds the organisations, the UCI and everything accountable to some very strict rules that makes sure the safety of the riders is held as a priority."

The UCI has been contacted by BBC Sport for comment.

Earlier this month the UCI proposed the introduction of GPS trackers at all races to pinpoint riders' locations at all times.

The sport's biggest races, such as the three-week Tour de France, typically have a good safety record. This is thanks in part to extensive safety measures which include total road closures on stages for much of the day.

Smaller events such as the Volta a Portugal and Tour of Britain use 'rolling roadblocks', where police and officials travel in front of and behind the peloton.

Races such as the third-tier Volta a Portugal sell their rights to be broadcast at a lower fee than the bigger races and use more cost-effective measures to manage road closures.

However, Brennan, who also won the prestigious one-day classic race Kuurne-Brussels-Kuurne this year, believes the demands of the sport are changing as it grows, and was vocal at the recent Vuelta over racing in 44-degree heat.

"We have big outside factors such as TV ... I would say that's a massive one. The instances of racing in Spain, and instead of moving it forward to racing at 09:00 we're racing at 15:00 in the midday heat.

"I think a real independent organisation that can really say to the teams whether something is safe, or whether something needs to be changed would benefit the sport and hopefully would stop these sad tragic events that happened at World Championships [referring to Muriel Furrer in 2024] and what happened with Fin and all the other sad events that happen in the sport."

title: Canada captain loses sleep 'four to five nights a week' over England's World Cup win
description: Canada captain Sophie de Goede says she still loses sleep over their World Cup final loss to England last year.
fullText:
It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone.

"Four to five nights a week I can't fall asleep because I'm still thinking about the final," says Canada captain Sophie de Goede, who is preparing to take on the world champions this Saturday at Sandy Park in Exeter.

So, is this match revenge for the side ranked third in the world?

Canada head coach Kevin Rouet is keen to play this down: "Revenge is a good brand but they [England] won the final of the World Cup - that was the most important game to win, the next important games will be in the World Cup 2029."

After Canada, England play New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, before two more tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa. In recent history, England's women have never faced such tough successive opposition.

Red Roses head coach John Mitchell says the games are an "audition" for the 2029 World Cup.

"You look at the geography that we're going to cover, we're not always going to be in our training base. We're going to be going to different facilities. It's a challenge," he said.

"It's going to be really cool to see how they handle pressure as well. I think the Red Roses are very good around pressure because I think it reveals how much they care".

Saturday, 19 September at 15:00 BST

There continues to be misconceptions around the status of the Canadian women: they are professional athletes but contracts, as with most other nations, do not yet compare to England's women.

The Canadian programme involves a clever strategy of using England's domestic PWR league to develop its players.

There are 25 Canadians in PWR and the current Canada coaching staff includes Kevin Rouet and Alex Austerberry, who both coach Saracens Women, and Nathan Smith from Loughborough Lightning.

"It's not like we're coming in to spy," joked De Goede. "We just don't have the quality league [in Canada]."

Canada are not the only country to do this - PWR is littered with top internationals from across the globe.

Mitchell has told BBC Sport that he and Charlie Hayter, head of women's performance at England Rugby, have lobbied to increase PWR game time for English Qualified Players (EQP) from next season.

Mitchell has frequently pushed his theory that players who can reach 1,000 PWR playing minutes a season "gives them a higher probability" of playing for the Red Roses.

"I haven't enjoyed seeing young English players between 21 and 23 not getting enough minutes," he said.

"I think that number [1,000] is very meaningful."

The RFU confirmed to BBC Sport the current requirements around 13 EQP players on average across matchday squads will remain. However, the lure of signing foreign talent will be dampened by the removal of club injury credit, which helps cover the cost of replacing an injured player.

From the 2027-28 season, only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible.

Besides this, if any EQP player is captured by another union, they will only be able to hold their EQP status until the end of that season.

title: I have experienced racism a thousand times - Lamine Yamal
description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism "a thousand times", because people are unaware their comments or behaviour are offensive.
fullText:
Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism "a thousand times", because people are unaware their comments or behaviour are offensive.

The Spanish Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia, a government agency, said earlier this year that the 19-year-old and Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr were the most frequent targets of online racist abuse in Spain in the final quarter of 2025.

Lamine Yamal was among the Barca players targeted by racist abuse during El Clasico against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu in October 2024.

And in an interview with broadcaster Movistar, the winger, who helped Spain to win the World Cup in July, said he had encountered racism on a regular basis during his rise to prominence.

"A thousand times. People are indirectly racist toward you, but maybe don't realise it," he said.

"There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist and they don't even notice.

He added: "If someone calls me Black, it's not going to bother me at all, ultimately I'm Black, I'm not any other colour.

"Another thing is whether it's good or bad, whether they're saying it to offend me.

"But if I'm playing a match and they paid for a ticket to see me, I'm not going to get angry just because they disrespected me."

title: Gabriel, 15, in Barcelona amid speculation over future
description: Man Utd youngster JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.
fullText:
Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has travelled to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.

The 15-year-old has told United he wants to cancel his registration with immediate effect.

BBC Sport reported on Thursday that Real Madrid have a firm interest in the forward, and Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain and Barcelona are also known to be keen.

It is understood Gabriel left the UK on Thursday and went to France, but is now in Barcelona.

If United hold on to the Londoner's registration, it would stop him moving to another English club until the end of the season.

But if he obtains a European Union passport through either his father - a former Republic of Ireland international - or mother, who has Greek-Cypriot heritage, he could join a club in the EU when he turns 16 on 6 October.

What next for Gabriel and Man Utd?

Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September. Tournament rules prevent him from playing for a side other than United in this season's competition.

Sources close to Gabriel were furious the club did not register him for their Champions League opener with Sabah FK, which Michael Carrick's side won 4-0.

The United manager was again asked about Gabriel on Friday at his news conference to preview Sunday's Premier League match against Fulham.

"He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important we don't play anything out here," he said.

"With the exposure and scrutiny and everything, you got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

"The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing."

Gabriel scored in his first two Premier League 2 outings for United this season but will not be involved against Brentford at Leigh Sports Village on Friday.

title: Ronaldo named in Jesus' first Portugal squad
description: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.
fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, ending speculation the 41-year-old could retire from international football.

Ronaldo refused to confirm whether he would continue to play for his country after Portugal's World Cup round-of-16 defeat by eventual winners Spain in July.

But the Al-Nassr forward is part of a 25-man group chosen for Portugal's four Nations League games between 24 September and 4 October.

Jesus has replaced Roberto Martinez, who stepped down as Portugal coach after their World Cup exit.

The 72-year-old was Ronaldo's club boss last season, when the pair helped Al-Nassr win the Saudi Pro League for the first time in seven years.

The former Manchester United Real Madrid forward, who announced that this summer's World Cup would be his last, was in tears after Portugal's World Cup exit.

When asked if he would keep playing for his country, he said: "I will meet the family and take decisions with a calm head."

This sparked speculation he could follow his great rival Lionel Messi and retire from international football.

Ronaldo will turn 42 before next summer's Nations League finals and will be 43 by Euro 2028.

title: 'Not a catastrophe' - Carrick dismisses Man Utd job fears
description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says there is no point wasting any time worrying if his job is under threat.
fullText:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick says it would be "ridiculous" to start thinking how long he has left in the job after "two or three" bad results.

His side visit Fulham on Sunday after an awful week.

After United lost at home to a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men after 23 minutes, Brighton became the first side to come from two goals down to win at Old Trafford in 50 years in their Carabao Cup tie.

United supporters responded to the midweek setback with boos and by chanting against their team.

Carrick said in the aftermath he was "not bothered" by the pressure - a sentiment he reinforced as he spoke to the media before the Fulham trip.

"I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing to a certain standard and achieving certain things on the pitch," he added.

"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's totally not in my thinking. It's ridiculous to think that way in the position I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

"It's two or three games. It's two or three games too many because I really hate losing, but that doesn't mean the world caves in. In some minds it does, it can't for us."

There has been no sense from senior figures inside United that Carrick's position is under threat. They are more focused on the perceived under performance of so many players given the 12 games out of 17 that were won under the 45-year-old over the second half of last season.

"It's not a catastrophe or a disaster," said Carrick. "It's not the end of the world."

Yet it is the measure of the noise around a club of United's size that is often feels that way.

Carrick accepted issues at Old Trafford are frequently amplified, so they look to be bigger than they actually are.

Despite this, he loves his job - and the club he served with such distinction as a player, and began his coaching career.

"There's great feelings, and there's obviously disappointments, and sometimes the smaller disappointments lead to being a little bit bigger," he added. "It's just part of coping and being at this great football club.

"I wouldn't want to be anywhere else, genuinely.

"It's the best place for me to be, in part because of the times when it's maybe not going to plan. Sometimes they are best times to work your way through, to find out a few things and come out an awful lot stronger."

Externally, the inquests have tended to focus around recruitment - or lack of it, specifically at left-back - United's finances and debt levels, Carrick's relative inexperience and, other than assistant boss Steve Holland, that of his coaches.

"It's not a blame game," said Carrick, who revealed Luke Shaw and new signing Carlos Baleba "have a chance" of being fit for the Craven Cottage meeting.

"We all search for things to look at and point at, or whatever reason it may be and find a blame. Blame me. No problem. I will take the responsibility.

"But it's not about blaming people. It's about us, it's about us finding solutions and being better. That's as a whole football club."

title: Oxford apologise for United 93 shirt advert
description: Oxford United apologises for the image, which features the call sign of one of the planes used in the 9/11 attacks.
fullText:
A football club has apologised after it published images of a new clothing line with "United 93" printed on the back - the call sign of one of the aircraft hijacked on 9/11.

The clothing was supposed to make reference to Oxford United's founding year of 1893.

However, it said it had been released "without understanding of the historical context and associations".

United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all 44 people on board after being hijacked on 11 September 2001. A docudrama film titled United 93 was made about the tragedy and released in 2006.

Oxford United was founded in 1893 as an amateur club called Headington and now plays in League One - the third tier of the English football pyramid.

In a statement, the club said its Campus Clothing range had been withdrawn and it "sincerely apologised" for the error.

"It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence," it said.

"We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again."

The 9/11 attacks saw 19 Al Qaeda members hijack four commercial passenger planes in the US.

Two of them were flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, resulting in them both collapsing.

Another plane struck the Pentagon, near Washington DC, while the fourth plane - United 93 - crashed in rural Pennsylvania. It was believed to be destined for the US Capitol Building, also in Washington DC.

The attacks killed 2,977 people and injured tens of thousands more.

title: Will England boss Tuchel 'embrace the chaos'?
description: After the World Cup, England boss Thomas Tuchel wanted greater control. Two months on, he is keen to "embrace the chaos" after naming his squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.
fullText:
England manager Thomas Tuchel left the United States in July pining for greater control.

At his first squad announcement since the World Cup on Friday, the German spoke of "embracing the chaos".

Is it possible to have controlled chaos? It seems Tuchel is ready to find out.

England's third-placed finish in the US was the nation's best performance at the World Cup since 1966.

But the memories of the team's semi-final loss to Argentina linger.

In the aftermath of the heartbreaking defeat, Tuchel pointed to his team's inability to find control having taken the lead via Anthony Gordon's opener as a key factor behind his side's late collapse.

Fast-forward two months, however, and the messaging is rather different ahead of the four upcoming Nations League games.

"Football is about adapting to situations and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach, if you look at the 6-4 against France [in the World Cup bronze-medal match]," said Tuchel.

"But people talk about it like it's one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match, so maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best."

Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning

Mixed signals? Or maybe it is just a sign that Tuchel wants his side to become more unpredictable in their search for success.

Because that is what the best teams do - mix it up when required.

Despite Tuchel's remarks, his latest squad for the fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia rather contradicts any thoughts of a havoc-rich approach.

The return of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer, two of English football's most technically gifted players, screams control.

So do the call-ups of Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, who are both extremely adept in possession of the ball.

Of course, there is certainly a balance to be struck. That would be Tuchel's ideal scenario.

Rio Ngumoha's first senior call-up will certainly add an air of unpredictability to Tuchel's options.

The Liverpool winger, 18, has had an exciting start to the season, catching the eye with his invention and trickery down both flanks for Andoni Iraola's side.

That Tuchel revealed Fulham attacker Josh King is also close to earning his first senior call-up provides further indication the England manager wants to reinvigorate his forward line ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign and beyond.

Yet, we shouldn't expect Tuchel to completely let go of the handbrake just yet.

In response to a question as to whether his team can replicate the fast-paced approach of a Premier League team but harnessed with a greater control, Tuchel responded: "That would be the wish, that we become for 10 minutes a little bit more like Spain, here and there.

"The more I reflect on it, it's maybe more buying into our strengths and play more minutes like we played the second half against Croatia, and more minutes like we played the first half against France, and buying into these strengths, because I think we get a lot of value out of it, we get a lot of connection to the fans, this is what the Premier League reflects.

"We are maybe not the most economical team to play football but this is maybe also a characteristic of the Premier League. The Premier League is not a very economical league, you have to play.

"You need to max out every single match otherwise you cannot compete for the title so this is something more beautiful. But this is where we are, where I am in my mindset and I think where the players are, so it's still a bit ambiguous."

But while Tuchel may not have total clarity with regards to whether control or chaos is the way forward, he showed no hint of confusion over who he believes his best players are.

Tuchel refuted assertions his decision to recall Palmer and Alexander-Arnold was an admission he'd got his World Cup squad wrong.

Indeed, Tuchel has hinted he would have picked a vastly similar squad for the upcoming games to the one he selected for the US had all his options been available.

"Before we did the nomination in the last month, I thought we had more of a continuation of the World Cup squad but then a lot of members of our World Cup squad - Reece [James], Dan [Burn], Dean [Henderson, [John] Stones, [Jordan] Henderson, Djed Spence - can't be with us due to injuries, so it is not like a full continuation.

"These players were crucial for us in building the brotherhood, in building the spirit and taking care of the mentality that took us the long way in the tournament. We will not negotiate on that, we will not give in on that.

"So other players will step up, this is basically how I see this camp.

"My mindset at the moment is not to change too much within the formations."

England host World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September then travel to the Czech Republic (Tuesday, 29 September) and Croatia (Saturday, 3 October) before the Czechs visit on Tuesday, 6 October.

'Resident Evil' review: Zach Cregger's video game adaptation is easily the best 'Resident Evil' movie yet
description:
Austin Abrams in Zach Cregger's Resident Evil.
Photo illustration: Yahoo News; photo: Sony Pictures Releasing/Everett...
fullText:
Ahead of the release of Zach Cregger's reboot today, there were already seven Resident Evil movies — six of them in a more action-oriented series starring Milla Jovovich, four of which were directed by her husband, Paul W.S. Anderson, plus an unrelated "reboot" in 2021 called Welcome to Raccoon City that went for more of a John Carpenter vibe and was an attempt to truly "adapt" the games. There's also a Netflix TV show version that ran for a single season in 2022. Countless other works in the horror genre have unofficially cribbed from the Resident Evil games over the years. It's an incredibly influential series.

And yet, Zach Cregger, hot off his Oscar-winning original horror film Weapons, is the first filmmaker to truly feel like he's adapting the experience of playing the games, arguably the scariest survival-horror ones ever made, rather than simply incorporating story and plot elements to explain the outbreak of infected people. In Cregger's hands, Resident Evil is pure crowd-pleasing popcorn cinema, best experienced in a packed movie theater with dozens of other people reacting loudly to the madness.

The premise couldn't be simpler — and the runtime a brisk 90ish minutes — as we follow a medical courier named Bryan (Austin Abrams, proving himself to be the Bruce Campbell for a new generation) who unwittingly finds himself fighting for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in a swirl of chaos. Fans of the video games will recognize various easter eggs and nods to game mechanics, including the importance of conserving ammo and checking every last drawer for more of it.

But you don't need to be familiar with the games at all to enjoy the movie, which is an efficient horror set-piece machine that just keeps putting Abrams in increasingly concerning situations. I can't stress enough how much this is a one-man show anchored by Abrams, and he crushes it. He's in every scene, earning tons of laughs simply by reacting as a normal person would in this situation; he's a true audience-surrogate character, ushering us through the chaos. His comedic timing, paired with Cregger's assured camerawork and editing, is a match made in genre-movie heaven.

I didn't expect it to be so heavily inspired by genre classics like The Thing and Evil Dead. In fact, it's a better Evil Dead movie than the last several movies with "Evil Dead" in the title, nailing the horror-comedy tone that only Sam Raimi and a few others can pull off with aplomb. Cregger has a ton of fun with the various monstrous forms that the infected take here, from fusing multiple humans together to crafting his own horror take on a big, scary guy like Dune's Baron Harkonnen. Resident Evil movies have thus far treated the zombies as pretty traditional movie zombies; Cregger's version gets at the attempt to create the next stage of human evolution.

title: Lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial says he 'didn't have any doubts'
description:
He was the sole holdout on a 12-person jury who otherwise voted to acquit Lindsay Clancy of murdering her three children — frustrating the defense and causing a mistrial.
After seven days of deliberations, and with specific instructions from Judge William Sullivan to follow the letter of the law on reasonable doubt, the jury said it still had one holdout who refused to budge. A mistrial was declared on Sept. 4.
Now, the lone juror, named Michael Desronvil, has come forward to share his side of the story, saying that he "didn't have any doubts" that Clancy was criminally responsible for the killings.
fullText:
He was the sole holdout on a 12-person jury who otherwise voted to acquit Lindsay Clancy of murdering her three children — frustrating the defense and causing a mistrial.

After seven days of deliberations, and with specific instructions from Judge William Sullivan to follow the letter of the law on reasonable doubt, the jury said it still had one holdout who refused to budge. A mistrial was declared on Sept. 4.

Now, the lone juror, named Michael Desronvil, has come forward to share his side of the story, saying that he "didn't have any doubts" that Clancy was criminally responsible for the killings.

In a statement shared with Yahoo News on Sept. 18 by his attorney Edward Andrew Paltzik, Desronvil said: "I didn't have any doubts. As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence presented.

"Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she (Clancy) knew exactly what she was doing and planned."

Desronvil refused to acquit Clancy on charges of the murder of her three children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan, whom she admitted killing in 2023.

Paltzik said in a social media post on Thursday that he was representing Desronvil and that his client would not be giving any interviews.

"We are focused entirely on his health, safety, and well-being," Paltzik said. "There will be a time for accountability and a time for the real story of the Lindsay Clancy Trial to be told. But not right now."

Paltzik added that his client was "safe and sound at an undisclosed secure location in a rural area of Northern New England."

The trial centered on whether Clancy could be held legally responsible for their deaths, as her defense argued that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time.

The case is scheduled to return to court on Sept. 29.

Desronvil's statement follows a number of jurors giving their views publicly about the case.

Last week, one juror said that Desronvil, one of three men serving on the jury, did not cite "a single piece of evidence" to support his position.

Juror Nick Dargie said the holdout juror did not show the other jurors any witness testimony or evidence to support his position.

"There was several times I would ask him to show us evidence or, you know, describe a witness testimony that helped to prove what he was saying, and ... he couldn't," Dargie said in an interview with ABC News aired on Sept. 10.

"There wasn't a single piece of evidence or witness testimony that he used to prove why he was thinking the way he was," Dargie continued, explaining that this was why the jury had given a note to Judge William Sullivan that eventually led to a mistrial.

"Otherwise, like, there's nothing wrong with somebody having a completely opposite opinion ... that would be a hung jury. That, like, that is our justice system."

Prior to Dargie's ABC interview, jury foreperson Roni Carlson had told NBC10 Boston that the holdout juror blocked Clancy's acquittal despite having reasonable doubt.

A guilty verdict requires guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, the highest standard of proof in the U.S. legal system.

"He had reasonable doubt. He admitted he had reasonable doubt," Carlson said.

"I started filling out the forms, I was so excited. There were three forms I had to fill out, and then he said, 'But I'm still not going to say that she's not guilty by reason of insanity.'"'

Another juror, who chose to remain anonymous, told local CBS station WBZ-TV that most of the jurors were "very firm in their stance," adding that "the stand-alone juror was not the only one that was unwilling to see things from the other side".

"I'm going to kind of defend that individual in a sense," she told WBZ-TV. "There were some big personalities in that room. But at the end of the day, it just came down to an inability to move past your convictions."

She added that there was "so much doubt."

"The prosecution didn't have a figurative smoking gun. There was not a single moment throughout the presentation of that case where you could say 'Yup, 100% I'm certain she did it' or that she didn't do it. There was too much gray area."

The two sides in the case are scheduled to return to court on Sept. 29, when the next steps will be decided.

Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz has not announced whether he will seek to retry Clancy.

Speaking outside the courthouse on Sept. 4 following the mistrial, Cruz said, "I appreciate the fact that there are strong feelings and opinions tied to this case."

He added: "However, our job is to set aside our feelings and focus solely on the facts. The facts are, Lindsay Clancy killed her three children and the evidence suggested to us that she was in control of her actions when she committed those homicides."

Meanwhile, Clancy's attorney, Kevin Reddington, said he was open to a plea deal, but told CNN's Anderson Cooper that he would not agree to one that would result in her serving prison time.

"I want to hear what Tim [Cruz] has to say," Reddington said. "I hope, however, after sitting through this trial and seeing the evidence that was presented from the government, as well as from the defense, that he would revisit that issue."

title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chair. His son will replace him.
description:

In his place as chair will be his son Howard G. Buffett, as has been telegraphed would happen for years.
fullText:
The final change of the guard at the storied Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B).

Berkshire Hathaway said Friday that Warren Buffett, 96, will step down as chairman effective immediately. He will move to the chairman emeritus role.

In his place as chair will be his son Howard G. Buffett, as has been telegraphed would happen for years.

Board life will now look much different for Howard, who has a striking resemblance to his legendary investor dad.

And Howard Buffett knows the transition will change his life, which has long consisted of frequent world travel for philanthropic ventures alongside a daily routine of being a farmer who tills his own land.

"I've been to 155 countries or something. And I'm on the road a lot. I've been in Ukraine five times in 2022. And the same thing, five times in 2023 and probably four or five times this year. So those are trips I won't make," Buffett told Yahoo Finance in a 2024 interview.

Buffett, 71, is seen as the "guardian" of the unique Berkshire culture that his father and longtime lieutenant Charlie Munger created over the decades. The business itself is a beast, requiring expert planning and oversight by the Berkshire board.

The business ranges from operating one of the nation's most important railroads in Burlington Northern to supporting the housing market via homebuilder Clayton Homes.

Buffett has an extensive management resume, from working in investor relations at commodities player Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) to serving as a board member of his dad's favorite drink and legacy stock investment, Coca-Cola (KO). (Howard retired from the Coke board in 2016 after 17 years.)

Buffett is also the chairman and CEO of the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, which was founded in 1999.

"I will need to keep in mind that I just need to be around to do my job [at Berkshire] and my responsibility. So I think the risk level of what I do in my life today probably gets decreased," Buffett said in the 2024 interview. "I won't be running the company as a non-executive chairman. My job will be to support [future CEO Greg Abel] in every way that I can."

title: His wife encouraged his 'American Idol' dream. Now he stands trial for her murder.
description:
Caleb Flynn appears in court on April 23, 2026, in Miami County, Ohio. - WHIO
About 13 years ago, “American Idol” contestant Caleb Flynn gushed about his wife Ashley, who he said encouraged him to audition for the 12th season of ABC’s singing competition.
“I love my wife more than anything,” he said in an interview during his brief stint on the show. “She’s very, very pretty, just – woof, I love her.”
Now, Flynn stands trial for her murder, as investigators allege the former music pastor fatally shot his wife of almost 16 years and staged the crime scene to make it appear she was killed by an intruder.
fullText:
About 13 years ago, “American Idol” contestant Caleb Flynn gushed about his wife Ashley, who he said encouraged him to audition for the 12th season of ABC’s singing competition.

“I love my wife more than anything,” he said in an interview during his brief stint on the show. “She’s very, very pretty, just – woof, I love her.”

Now, Flynn stands trial for her murder, as investigators allege the former music pastor fatally shot his wife of almost 16 years and staged the crime scene to make it appear she was killed by an intruder.

Flynn, 40, was arrested in February, days after he frantically called 911 to report someone broke into their Tipp City, Ohio, home and killed his wife – a beloved middle school volleyball coach – while he was in their daughters’ bedroom.

“We’re looking forward to trying the case,” his defense attorney, Patrick Mulligan, told CNN Tuesday. “We’ve been waiting for this.”

Flynn has pleaded not guilty to charges of aggravated murder, murder, felonious assault, and tampering with evidence.

The murder trial, which is slated to last about two weeks, started with jury selection on Thursday. Sixteen panelists – four of whom have been designated alternates – were seated, according to CNN affiliate WHIO. Opening statements are expected Friday morning.

During the proceedings, the jurors are expected to visit the family’s home to view the crime scene and hear testimony from several of Ashley’s family members – including the couple’s preteen daughters, who are crucial to their father’s presumed alibi.

Prosecutors have provided scant details about the investigation and have not yet offered a purported motive for the killing or described the alleged “cover up” – key components jurors will likely consider during their deliberations.

“It will become apparent what the status of the evidence is as things go on,” Mulligan told CNN, adding he didn’t believe the prosecution would be able to prove the charges beyond a reasonable doubt. He previously suggested authorities had made a “rush to judgment” in arresting his client.

“When the government runs out of leads or can’t develop leads and looks at a surviving spouse in cases such as these, the chance of a wrongful conviction increases,” the defense attorney said in a statement to The Associated Press shortly after Flynn’s arrest in February.

If the panel convicts Flynn of the most serious charge, he could be sentenced to life in prison without parole.

Weeks before the trial’s start, Judge Jeannine Pratt denied a defense motion to change the venue of the trial and a motion from prosecutors to sequester the jury, with both parties arguing the high public interest in the case could jeopardize the impartiality of the panel.

The court will impose additional measures to ensure jurors are impartial, Pratt wrote in her ruling, and may reconsider the parties’ requests if any issues arise while seating the jury.

In the early morning hours of February 16, Ashley was shot and killed inside the suburban home she shared with her husband and their two daughters.

Caleb Flynn told investigators he was sleeping in the living room that night because he had a bad cough, according to a conversation captured on police body-worn cameras. He woke up when he heard one of their dogs moving, he said, and assumed one of the children had gotten out of bed.

“I went in their room, and I laid down with them for – I don’t even know how long, and that’s when I heard it,” Flynn told the officers, saying he “froze” when he heard a gunshot.

“When I finally got up, the door leading to the garage was open, but I didn’t see anybody,” he said.

In a 911 call around 2:30 a.m., Flynn reported an intruder had broken into the house and shot his wife.

“My wife, she’s got two shots to her head. There’s blood everywhere,” he said breathlessly. “Oh my God, oh my God, oh my God.”

Footage from police body cameras showed first responders rushing into the family’s home shortly after and clearing the house with their guns drawn.

“We have a lady with a gunshot wound to the head in her bed,” one officer said. “We got gun casings on the floor. The husband’s here and the kids are here.”

While searching through the garage, police noted a door leading outside was open, as was the center console in a parked truck. Flynn told investigators he had a few guns in the house, including a handgun he stored in his truck, according to the footage.

As officers secured the scene over the next hour, police bodycam footage captured Flynn sobbing, calling loved ones and appearing to vomit. When Ashley’s mother arrived at the home, he fell to his knees, wailing, before they embraced on the front lawn.

“The girls don’t know, the girls are sleeping,” Flynn said as he hugged her. “I don’t know what to do, I don’t know what to do, I don’t know what to do.”

“I don’t know what to do either,” the grandmother said through tears. “I’m just – I’m in shock.”

That night, Flynn agreed to go to the police station to provide a statement about the incident, the bodycam footage shows. “You’ll be riding up front with me,” an officer told him as he pointed to a nearby car.

Three days later, Flynn was handcuffed in the back of a police vehicle on his way to the Miami County Jail, where he’s been held since his arrest. His bond was set at $3.5 million.

Initial charging documents said officers were at first “lead estray (sic) by the staging of the crime scene,” though authorities have not provided details about the alleged cover-up.

“As a result of the investigation, probable cause existed to charge Caleb Flynn with the murder of his wife,” Tipp City police said in a news release announcing his arrest. “Due to the ongoing nature of this case, specific investigative details will not be released at this time.”

Ashley’s family believes the arrest was made “carefully and not without serious consideration,” according to a statement shared with CNN affiliate WKEF.

“After speaking with both local police and federal authorities, we trust the proper steps were taken and the process is being handled appropriately,” they wrote. “We kindly ask for privacy as we work through this complex situation.”

In the aftermath of her shocking death, the suburban community of Tipp City – just north of Dayton – came together to mourn Ashley, a beloved substitute teacher and volleyball coach.

Ribbons and Bible verses adorned the downtown streets in her memory, and local restaurants donated some of their proceeds to her family, according to CNN affiliate WHIO.

“She was such a pillar to the community,” neighbor Tia Turner told WKEF. “She was one of the first people to welcome us in the neighborhood.”

About a week after her death, Ashley’s friends and family commemorated what would have been her 38th birthday. Her daughters blew out candles on chocolate cupcakes, WKEF reported, and her loved ones released balloons with handwritten messages into the sky.

“We miss her in ways words can’t capture. But we hold tightly to this: Ashley’s life was always about pointing people to Jesus and showing them His love,” her family said in a statement provided to WKEF.

“And her legacy will live on – in her daughters, in her parents, in her sister, and in the many lives she touched and influenced along the way.”

title: A Chinese woman crossed the border for a concert. It could cost her family their welfare.
description:
Illuminated buildings in Central district in Hong Kong, China, on Sunday, Jun. 21, 2026. - Paul Yeung/Bloomberg/Getty Images
A woman from a low-income family in China crossed over into Hong Kong to get to a concert she had spent months saving up for.
It was a trip that Beijing’s vast surveillance apparatus didn’t miss. Now her family face the prospect of losing their government benefits for splurging on “high-end consumption.
fullText:
A woman from a low-income family in China crossed over into Hong Kong to get to a concert she had spent months saving up for.

It was a trip that Beijing’s vast surveillance apparatus didn’t miss. Now her family face the prospect of losing their government benefits for splurging on “high-end consumption.”

The incident has sparked massive debate across Chinese social media over whether those receiving benefits are also entitled to small luxuries. It’s also a reminder of the staggering extent of the Chinese government’s surveillance system, one turbocharged by advances in AI and the embrace of digital payments.

The story first surfaced in a post on popular site Red Note in early September by a user who said they were the young woman’s cousin.

The woman, surnamed Huang, had “worked hard doing manual labor and saved up from the subsidies” to pay for the concert ticket and expenses of traveling to Hong Kong, around 235 miles (380 kilometers) from her home in Jiangxi province, the post said.

That post has since been taken down, but Chinese officials have said it was indeed written by the woman’s cousin. A screenshot of it has also been used by state media reporting on the case.

Hong Kong was handed back to China in 1997 following more than 100 years of British colonial rule. It is governed by separate legal and political systems to mainland China, and mainland Chinese citizens still must apply for permission to travel there.

According to the Red Note post, a local social worker warned Huang before the trip that any border crossing could trigger a review of her family’s eligibility for welfare.

“I can’t tell if she was actually dumb enough to think Hong Kong doesn’t count as going abroad, or if she knew perfectly well and went anyway,” it said.

The family is in “extreme, extreme poverty” and the prospect of losing the payments has left them in “complete devastation,” the post said.

It is unclear what concert Huang had risked so much to go and see.

For many of the legions of K-Pop fans in mainland China, Hong Kong is the most accessible place to see a K-Pop concert. For the past decade, Beijing has placed an unofficial ban on performances by Korean artists on the mainland as it feuds with Seoul over trade and the presence of US weapons in South Korea.

In late August in Hong Kong there was a two-day international music awards festival featuring performances from different K-Pop bands, including some famous ones such as ALLDAY PROJECT, aespa, BABYMONSTER, RIIZE, Super Junior and TOMORROW X TOGETHER.

On September 7, the Social Affairs Management Bureau in Ganzhou in Jiangxi province, where the young woman lives, issued an official readout on its website in response to the heated discussion on the original Red Note post.

The bureau said Huang and her family were under investigation “after she independently traveled to Hong Kong to attend a concert, the trip triggered an alert in the dynamic monitoring system for recipients of the minimum living allowance.”

The city’s New Economic Development Zone’s Social Affairs Management Bureau told CNN on Wednesday that the investigation is ongoing.

Over the four decades to 2020, China lifted the vast bulk of its population out of poverty, and in 2021 leader Xi Jinping declared that extreme poverty had been eliminated. But official data shows around 40 million people across the country still depend on government living subsidies.

According to Ganzhou’s policy, if a household per-person income is below the minimum living allowance threshold set by the government, each person in the family could receive 1,005 yuan per month, equivalent to $150 dollars.

The case has sparked so much debate that China’s state media has waded in.

The Communist Party mouthpiece People’s Daily issued a commentary last week saying “of course, reasonable freedom to spend one’s money should be respected, but that freedom has limits, and people receiving public assistance are even more obligated to follow the rules.”

Government basic living subsidies are “meant to cover basic necessities such as food, clothing, housing, and transportation. Going to Hong Kong to see a concert is a high-cost form of entertainment, so there is nothing unreasonable about it triggering an alert in the monitoring system,” it said.

The online discussion has drawn over 120 million views on Chinese social media platform Weibo. Some commenters said they thought it would be “cruel” if the family lost their welfare. “Does being low-income mean you are not allowed to enjoy things you like?,” asked one person.

But many other were less sympathetic. “Her family is struggling this badly, and she doesn’t think to use the money she earns to help her family out?” asked another user of the platform.

description:
